Builds a unified benchmark with consistent resizing, padding, quantization, and metric code across CEILNet, Real20, Postcard, Objects, and Wild datasets.
AI.result: Achieves macro-average of 27.546 dB PSNR, 0.9220 SSIM, 0.9751 NCC, and 0.004760 LMSE across five datasets, outperforming all compared public checkpoints and internal variants on macro-average PSNR, SSIM, and NCC, and achieving lowest LMSE.
AI.conclusion: The main benefit is more balanced performance across diverse reflection distributions; clear semantic reflections in Postcard remain a challenging case.

title: An Integrated Deep Learning and Statistical Framework for Whole-Network Gene--Environment Association with Leaf Vascular Architecture
summary: Leaf veins exhibit remarkable diversity in architecture and patterning, yet existing gene--environment association studies have primarily quantified leaf venation using a small collection of low-dimensional summary traits, thereby discarding most of the structural information contained in the original images. We propose an integrated deep learning and statistical framework. The proposed framework achieves four methodological advances. First, it represents the complete leaf vascular architecture as a whole-network image phenotype. Second, it fine-tunes the deep learning-based Edge Detection with Transformers (EDTER) model to accurately extract whole-network leaf vascular architecture from RGB images by jointly learning local and global contextual features. Third, it constructs a new annotated leaf image database by integrating edge maps generated by DiffusionEdge with the Berkeley Segmentation Database (BSDS500). Fourth, it applies Semiparametric Sparse Canonical Correlation Analysis (SSCCA) to perform variable selection and model associations between repeatedly measured high-dimensional Bivariate image responses and high-dimensional predictors while simultaneously accommodating sparse, zero-inflated data represented by edge maps through a truncated latent Gaussian copula model. Two simulation studies demonstrate the performance of the proposed framework under increasing levels of complexity. Application to a real \emph{Populus} dataset identifies three significant gene--geography interactions associated with leaf vascular architecture, providing new biological insights and establishing a broadly applicable methodological framework for high-dimensional complex image phenotypes.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes an integrated deep learning and statistical framework to analyze leaf vascular architecture as whole-network image phenotypes, using Edge Detection with Transformers (EDTER), a new annotated leaf image database, and Semiparametric Sparse Canonical Correlation Analysis (SSCCA) to identify gene-environment associations, validated through simulations and a real Populus dataset.
AI.motivation: Existing gene-environment association studies quantify leaf venation using low-dimensional summary traits, discarding most structural information from original images; there is a need to capture the complete leaf vascular architecture as high-dimensional image phenotypes.
AI.method: (1) Representing leaf vascular architecture as whole-network image phenotypes; (2) Fine-tuning EDTER to extract vascular networks from RGB images via joint local-global contextual learning; (3) Constructing a new annotated leaf image database using DiffusionEdge edge maps and BSDS500; (4) Applying SSCCA for variable selection and association modeling between high-dimensional bivariate image responses and predictors, using a truncated latent Gaussian copula to handle sparse, zero-inflated edge map data.
AI.result: Simulation studies demonstrate performance under increasing complexity. Application to a real Populus dataset identifies three significant gene-geography interactions associated with leaf vascular architecture.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides new biological insights into leaf venation genetics and establishes a broadly applicable methodology for analyzing high-dimensional complex image phenotypes.

title: SF-AMS: Strategic Forgetting for Structured Memory in LLM Agent
summary: Managing long-context dependencies remains a primary bottleneck in LLM agents, as redundant and irrelevant information can degrade multi-step reasoning. Strategic Forgetting for Agent Memory Systems (SF-AMS) is proposed as a framework for maintaining compact high-utility memory by modeling the long-term importance of memory units. SF-AMS replaces static retrieval and heuristic decay with a utility-driven survival mechanism that updates memory importance from usage redundancy and temporal signals, inducing a hierarchical memory structure that prioritizes stable entity-consistent information while filtering noise. On top of this, Composite Importance Scoring integrates semantic and entity level signals to improve retrieval robustness. Experiments on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-s show consistent gains over strong state of the art baselines including LightMem MemO and A-Mem. The largest improvement appears in multi-hop reasoning under Qwen2.5-7B where SF-AMS achieves plus 9.65 F1 over the strongest baseline followed by temporal reasoning under GPT-4o-mini plus 6.91 F1 and open-domain tasks plus 6.53 F1 demonstrating strong cross backbone generalization. These results show that modeling memory importance as a dynamic utility signal is critical for reliable long-context reasoning.

AI.tldr: SF-AMS is a framework that strategically forgets unimportant information in LLM agent memory by modeling long-term importance via utility-driven survival, achieving consistent gains (up to +9.65 F1) over baselines on long-context reasoning tasks.
AI.motivation: Long-context dependencies remain a bottleneck for LLM agents due to redundant/irrelevant information degrading multi-step reasoning; existing static retrieval and heuristic decay methods are insufficient.
AI.method: SF-AMS replaces static retrieval and heuristic decay with a utility-driven survival mechanism that updates memory importance from usage redundancy and temporal signals, inducing a hierarchical memory structure. Composite Importance Scoring integrates semantic and entity-level signals for retrieval robustness.
AI.result: Consistent gains over LightMem, MemO, A-Mem; largest improvement in multi-hop reasoning under Qwen2.5-7B (+9.65 F1), temporal reasoning under GPT-4o-mini (+6.91 F1), open-domain (+6.53 F1).
AI.conclusion: Modeling memory importance as a dynamic utility signal is critical for reliable long-context reasoning in LLM agents.

title: On AI Safety and Security Technical Debt in Engineering AI-Enabled Systems
comment: 64 pages, 7 figures, 8 tables, submitted to ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology (TOSEM)
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly deployed in high-stakes domains such as healthcare, autonomous driving, finance, and education. While these systems offer powerful data-driven and adaptive capabilities, their complexity, rapid evolution, and dependence on dynamic data pipelines introduce new forms of engineering liability collectively referred to as AI Technical Debts (AITDs). AITDs arise from root causes spanning data governance, model implementation, algorithm design, architectural decisions, operational processes, documentation practices, and testing adequacy. Unlike conventional technical debt, many AITDs are latent and propagate across tightly coupled AI pipelines, leading to maintenance challenges, reliability degradation, and heightened safety or security risks. Guided by the principles of AI Trust, Risk, and Security Management (AI TRiSM), this study reinterprets technical debt through the interconnected dimensions of trustworthiness, focusing on AI safety and security technical debts. We conduct a systematic review of 60 primary studies and identify 31 distinct types of AITD, which are organized into a root-cause-oriented taxonomy comprising seven classes. The analysis examines how these debts map to 18 trust-related concerns, including 6 safety hazards and 12 security vulnerabilities. To support mitigation, the review synthesizes 34 actionable guidelines (8 safety and 26 security) targeting the prevention, detection, and reduction of AITDs across the AI lifecycle. Building on these findings, we introduce AITD-MAP, an integrated framework that connects the AITD taxonomy, quality and risk impacts, and mitigation strategies into a unified structure for risk-aware AI engineering. The framework aims to assist AI software engineers in making AI safety and security technical debts visible, understanding their root causes, and mitigating their presence.

AI.tldr: This paper systematically reviews 60 studies on AI Technical Debts (AITDs), identifying 31 types organized into a 7-class root-cause taxonomy, mapping them to 18 trust-related concerns (6 safety hazards, 12 security vulnerabilities), and proposing 34 mitigation guidelines (8 safety, 26 security). The authors introduce AITD-MAP, an integrated framework connecting taxonomy, impacts, and strategies for risk-aware AI engineering.
AI.motivation: AI systems deployed in high-stakes domains introduce new forms of engineering liability (AITDs) that, unlike conventional technical debt, are often latent and propagate across coupled AI pipelines. Existing approaches lack a structured understanding of these debts from a trust, risk, and security management perspective.
AI.method: Systematic review of 60 primary studies following AI TRiSM principles, resulting in a root-cause-oriented taxonomy of 31 AITD types across 7 classes, mapped to 18 trust-related concerns (6 safety hazards, 12 security vulnerabilities), and synthesis of 34 actionable mitigation guidelines.
AI.result: Identified 31 distinct AITD types organized into 7 root-cause classes; mapped to 6 safety hazards and 12 security vulnerabilities; synthesized 34 mitigation guidelines (8 safety, 26 security); developed AITD-MAP framework.
AI.conclusion: AITD-MAP provides a unified structure to make AI safety and security technical debts visible, understand their root causes, and guide mitigation, supporting risk-aware AI engineering across the AI lifecycle.

title: Neural Representation of Minimal Surfaces
summary: We propose a neural representation for minimal surfaces. Unlike prior approaches based on discretization or Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), where meshes or neural fields are optimized to approximate the governing equations, our method builds on an exact representation, similar to the classical Weierstrass--Enneper parameterization, yielding minimal surfaces up to negligible quadrature error in evaluation. We formulate a training objective for the Plateau problem that optimizes over this representation.

AI.tldr: A neural representation for minimal surfaces is proposed that, unlike discretization or PINN-based methods, uses an exact representation akin to the Weierstrass–Enneper parameterization, achieving minimal surfaces with negligible quadrature error; the training objective for the Plateau problem is formulated to optimize over this representation.
AI.motivation: To overcome approximation errors and discretization limitations in existing methods (e.g., PINNs, mesh-based approaches) for computing minimal surfaces by developing an exact neural representation.
AI.method: The authors propose a neural representation inspired by the classical Weierstrass–Enneper parameterization. Instead of directly solving PDEs via PINNs or mesh discretization, they encode the exact mathematical structure of minimal surfaces into a neural network, and optimize over this representation to solve the Plateau problem.
AI.result: The proposed method yields minimal surfaces up to negligible quadrature error in evaluation, significantly improving accuracy over prior approaches that rely on discretization or PINNs.
AI.conclusion: The exact neural representation offers a more accurate and principled framework for computing minimal surfaces, with potential advantages for the Plateau problem and related geometric tasks.

title: Disentangling Acoustic Cues in Alzheimer's Pathology and Perception: The Roles of Language and Gender
summary: Acoustic biomarkers show promise for detecting Alzheimer's Disease (AD), yet whether the cues driving diagnostic AI align with those salient to human listeners is underexplored across languages and genders, where pathological markers and perceptual strategies differ. We train models to predict clinical AD status (pathology) and human perceptual scores across Mandarin and Greek, male and female speakers. Using SHAP for interpretability and statistical models for validation, we compare feature importance by subgroup. Results reveal a context-dependent divergence: pathological-perceptual alignment is significant for Mandarin and female speakers but disappears for Greek and male speakers, where pathology models did not exceed chance; this is a failure mode that population-specific auditing surfaces. Global Explainable AI (XAI) explanations can mask critical demographic divergences, highlighting the need for population-specific explainability auditing for equitable deployment of clinical speech AI.

AI.tldr: This study examines whether AI diagnostic cues for Alzheimer's Disease align with human perceptual cues across languages and genders, finding significant alignment for Mandarin/female speakers but not for Greek/male speakers, highlighting the need for population-specific explainability auditing in clinical speech AI.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether the acoustic features driving AI-based Alzheimer's detection align with those perceived by human listeners, and how this alignment varies across different languages (Mandarin vs. Greek) and genders, addressing a gap in cross-linguistic and cross-gender explainability.
AI.method: Trained AI models to predict clinical AD status and human perceptual scores across Mandarin/Greek and male/female speakers. Used SHAP for interpretability and statistical models for validation, comparing feature importance across subgroups.
AI.result: Pathological-perceptual alignment was significant for Mandarin and female speakers but disappeared for Greek and male speakers. Pathology models for Greek and male speakers did not exceed chance performance.
AI.conclusion: Global XAI explanations can obscure critical demographic divergences. Population-specific explainability auditing is essential for equitable deployment of clinical speech AI.

title: StepX-Edge: An On-Device UI Vision-Language Model via Architecture-Training-Deployment Co-Design
summary: Deploying a vision-language model with full UI understanding on end devices has long been trapped between accuracy and efficiency: on one side is the accuracy bar for OCR, screen understanding, visual question answering, and element grounding; on the other is the strict compute, memory, and power budget of mobile chips. Existing work either trades one for the other, or stops at simulation without real-device validation. We present StepX-Edge, a 0.9B-parameter on-device UI vision-language model that resolves this tension through three-layer co-design of architecture, training, and deployment. Architecturally, UI-aware Layered Visual Encoding (ULVE) and a Progressive Dimensionality Projection (PDP) connector target the extreme aspect ratios and fine-grained perception of screens, while standard full attention throughout ensures native compatibility with mainstream mobile NPU operators. For training, the five-stage StepX-Curriculum framework is designed around our observation of mutual-promotion effects among UI subtasks, so that all four capabilities grow synergistically under a tight parameter budget rather than interfering. For deployment, a module-wise differentiated two-stage PTQ-to-QAT quantization scheme keeps the post-quantization accuracy loss within 1%. StepX-Edge achieves the strongest overall UI understanding among <=1B models, surpassing all 2B-2.3B baselines on ScreenQA (88.76 F1) and Chinese OCRBench v2 (57.25), and matching 1.3B-2.3B general VLMs on RefCOCO (92.0%) and OCRBench v1 (831) with far fewer parameters. After W4A16+KV8 quantization, the model runs stably on Snapdragon 8 Gen5 devices with ~0.84 s TTFT, 98 tok/s decode, and 1.4 GB peak memory. We will open-source the training data, the full training recipe, and the quantization deployment pipeline.

AI.tldr: StepX-Edge is a 0.9B-parameter on-device UI vision-language model that achieves strong UI understanding (OCR, screen understanding, VQA, element grounding) on mobile devices through three-layer co-design of architecture (ULVE + PDP connector), training (five-stage StepX-Curriculum), and deployment (two-stage PTQ-to-QAT quantization). It matches or surpasses larger models (1.3B-2.3B) on benchmarks while running efficiently on Snapdragon 8 Gen5 (~0.84s TTFT, 98 tok/s, 1.4GB peak memory).
AI.motivation: Deploying vision-language models with full UI understanding on end devices faces a fundamental tension between accuracy (OCR, screen understanding, VQA, element grounding) and efficiency (compute, memory, and power constraints of mobile chips). Existing work either sacrifices one for the other or lacks real-device validation.
AI.method: The model uses three-layer co-design: (1) Architecture: UI-aware Layered Visual Encoding (ULVE) and Progressive Dimensionality Projection (PDP) connector for extreme aspect ratios and fine-grained perception, with full attention for NPU compatibility; (2) Training: five-stage StepX-Curriculum framework leveraging mutual-promotion effects among UI subtasks; (3) Deployment: module-wise differentiated two-stage PTQ-to-QAT quantization limiting accuracy loss to within 1%.
AI.result: StepX-Edge achieves strongest overall UI understanding among ≤1B models, surpassing 2B-2.3B baselines on ScreenQA (88.76 F1) and Chinese OCRBench v2 (57.25), and matching 1.3B-2.3B models on RefCOCO (92.0%) and OCRBench v1 (831). After W4A16+KV8 quantization, it runs on Snapdragon 8 Gen5 with ~0.84s TTFT, 98 tok/s decode, and 1.4GB peak memory.
AI.conclusion: The three-layer co-design successfully resolves the accuracy-efficiency trade-off for on-device UI VLMs, achieving state-of-the-art performance at ≤1B scale with real-device deployment feasibility. The authors will open-source training data, recipe, and quantization pipeline.

title: Beyond Shapley: An Influence-Based Data Auditing Pipeline for LLM Alignment and Evaluation
summary: The alignment of Large Language Models (LLMs) is increasingly bottlenecked by data quality. As datasets scale, massive preference and instruction-tuning corpora inevitably accumulate hidden structural contradictions, safety risks, and systemic human annotation errors. Standard dataset auditing methods, such as semantic deduplication or LLM-as-a-judge, struggle to capture the actual predictive impact of individual records and often miss deep functional rule clashes. To address this, we introduce a scalable, inference-only data valuation pipeline that approximates the Shapley value without iterative model retraining. By mapping semantic k-NN neighborhoods into a directed graph, our framework evaluates data utility directly through a reference LLM's probability distribution using zero-shot and one-shot conditional log-likelihood shifts. Our pipeline then translates these predictive influence scores into localized advantage metrics to isolate gradient-conflicting records. We demonstrate the pipeline's efficacy in sanitizing two heavily vetted alignment datasets. First, applying our pipeline to the HelpSteer2 dataset reduced the manual audit search space by 99.1%, successfully uncovering falsely-labeled records across diverse failure modes. Second, applying our automated audit strategy to Anthropic's HH-RLHF training and evaluation splits identified thousands of hidden safety and factual preference inversions. Crucially, by extending this audit to the evaluation split, we expose severe vulnerabilities in current benchmark integrity: highly capable models frequently predict the safer or more helpful response, only to be penalized by objectively flawed human ground-truth labels. Overall, our work provides a mathematically grounded, highly efficient diagnostic tool to uncover human label failures, sanitize evaluation benchmarks, and ensure the integrity of LLM alignment data.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a scalable, inference-only data valuation pipeline that approximates Shapley values without retraining, using semantic k-NN graphs and conditional log-likelihood shifts to detect problematic records in LLM alignment datasets. It reduces manual audit search space by 99.1% on HelpSteer2 and uncovers thousands of hidden safety and factual preference inversions in HH-RLHF, revealing flawed ground-truth labels in evaluation benchmarks.
AI.motivation: LLM alignment is bottlenecked by data quality; massive preference and instruction-tuning datasets contain hidden structural contradictions, safety risks, and systematic human annotation errors that standard auditing methods (semantic deduplication, LLM-as-a-judge) fail to capture, as they cannot measure the actual predictive impact of individual records.
AI.method: A scalable inference-only data valuation pipeline that approximates Shapley values without iterative model retraining. It maps semantic k-NN neighborhoods into a directed graph and evaluates data utility through a reference LLM's probability distribution using zero-shot and one-shot conditional log-likelihood shifts. These predictive influence scores are translated into localized advantage metrics to isolate gradient-conflicting records.
AI.result: On HelpSteer2, the pipeline reduced manual audit search space by 99.1% and uncovered falsely-labeled records across diverse failure modes. On Anthropic's HH-RLHF, it identified thousands of hidden safety and factual preference inversions in both training and evaluation splits, exposing that highly capable models frequently predict safer/more helpful responses yet are penalized by flawed human ground-truth labels.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a mathematically grounded, highly efficient diagnostic tool for uncovering human label failures, sanitizing evaluation benchmarks, and ensuring the integrity of LLM alignment data.

title: Synthetic Scenario Generation for Evaluation of Industry 4.0 Agents
summary: Industrial agent benchmarks require realistic evaluation scenarios that integrate telemetry, failure modes, maintenance records, and domain standards. However, existing benchmarks such as AssetOpsBench rely on manually authored scenarios and cover a limited set of asset classes. We extend AssetOpsBench with a Smart Grid Transformer asset class and four IEC-grounded diagnostic tools for health-index prediction, dissolved-gas analysis, winding-temperature assessment, and load-profile assessment. We further introduce ScenarioGeneratorAgent, a pipeline for synthetic industrial-agent scenario generation. The pipeline constructs evidence-grounded asset profiles, allocates coverage-aware scenario budgets across operational domains, and generates candidates through a hybrid validation-and-repair loop that enforces schema validity, tool reachability, physical plausibility, standards alignment, and deduplication. To improve scalability, we apply two-level caching, parallel focus-group generation, thread-pool offloading, batched LLM calls, and early rejection filtering. On Smart Grid Transformer scenario generation, these optimizations reduce end-to-end runtime by $8\times$ for 50 scenarios while preserving quality, achieving a composite quality score of $74.2 \pm 1.9$ compared with $73.8 \pm 3.0$ for the unoptimized baseline. These results show that standards-grounded synthetic scenario generation can efficiently expand industrial-agent benchmarks without sacrificing scenario quality.

AI.tldr: This paper extends AssetOpsBench with a Smart Grid Transformer asset class and IEC-grounded diagnostic tools, and introduces ScenarioGeneratorAgent—a pipeline for scalable synthetic scenario generation that reduces runtime by 8× while maintaining quality.
AI.motivation: Existing industrial agent benchmarks like AssetOpsBench rely on manually authored scenarios covering a limited set of asset classes, making them unscalable and hard to extend to new operational domains.
AI.method: The authors propose ScenarioGeneratorAgent, a pipeline that profiles asset evidence, allocates coverage-aware scenario budgets, and generates candidates via a hybrid validation-and-repair loop enforcing schema validity, tool reachability, physical plausibility, standards alignment, and deduplication. Scalability is improved via two-level caching, parallel focus-group generation, thread-pool offloading, batched LLM calls, and early rejection filtering.
AI.result: On Smart Grid Transformer scenario generation, optimizations reduce end-to-end runtime by 8× for 50 scenarios while achieving a composite quality score of 74.2±1.9 (vs. 73.8±3.0 baseline).
AI.conclusion: Standards-grounded synthetic scenario generation can efficiently expand industrial-agent benchmarks without sacrificing scenario quality.

title: TLA$^{+}$-Bench: An Execution-Grounded Benchmark and Dataset for Natural-Language to TLA+ Specification Generation
comment: 17 pages, appendix included. Introduces TLA+-Bench, an execution-grounded benchmark and dataset for natural-language to TLA$^{+}$ specification generation. Dataset, evaluation code, and model outputs available at publication
summary: Large language models increasingly write TLA$^{+}$ formal specifications from natural-language descriptions, but progress is hard to measure: existing resources grade by resemblance to a reference or by whether the output parses, neither of which shows correctness. We present TLA$^{+}$-Bench, a dataset and benchmark that grades by execution. Every gold specification ships a configuration the TLA$^{+}$ model checker runs over the full reachable state space, deciding exactly whether the specification holds the properties that configuration names. The dataset holds 403 model-checked gold and 897 parse-only silver specifications from 13 public repositories, subsumes prior TLA$^{+}$ generation data, and carries four model-written descriptions in two styles from two providers, with difficulty and category labels. Our main finding is about measurement itself: an exact oracle gives not one correctness number but a range. Varying only the grading choices earlier benchmarks leave unstated, on one fixed set of model outputs, the correct rate moves sixfold, from 10.0\% to 1.7\%; adding the interface-supply choice, where the model is told the configuration's names, widens the range to elevenfold, from 18.7\% to 1.7\%. We call this range the correctness envelope and measure each of its bounds. The findings inside it are stable. Every model writes valid TLA$^{+}$ far more often than correct TLA$^{+}$: the strongest is correct 16\% of the time by default and 26\% when given the interface names, open models at most 1\%, and correctness falls sharply with difficulty.

AI.tldr: TLA$^{+}$-Bench is a benchmark that grades TLA$^{+}$ specifications by execution on a model checker, revealing that varying grading choices can shift reported correctness rates six- to eleven-fold (from 18.7% to 1.7%), and that all models produce valid TLA$^{+}$ far more often than correct TLA$^{+}$ (best model: 16-26% correct; open models: ≤1%).
AI.motivation: Existing TLA$^{+}$ generation benchmarks grade by syntactic resemblance to a reference or by whether the output parses, neither of which measures actual semantic correctness. A more rigorous evaluation method is needed to track progress.
AI.method: The authors construct TLA$^{+}$-Bench with 403 model-checked gold specifications (each verified by the TLA$^{+}$ model checker over the full reachable state space) and 897 parse-only silver specifications from 13 public repositories. Four model-written descriptions in two styles from two providers are included, with difficulty and category labels. The benchmark reveals a "correctness envelope" by varying unstated grading choices across a fixed set of model outputs.
AI.result: Varying only grading choices that earlier benchmarks leave unstated, the correct rate moves sixfold (10.0% to 1.7%); adding the interface-supply choice expands the range to elevenfold (18.7% to 1.7%). The strongest model is correct 16% by default and 26% with interface names; open models achieve at most 1% correctness. Correctness declines sharply with difficulty.
AI.conclusion: Exact oracles for TLA$^{+}$ generation produce not a single correctness number but a range (the "correctness envelope"). All models write valid TLA$^{+}$ far more often than correct TLA$^{+}$, highlighting a critical gap between syntactic validity and semantic correctness.

title: TexSketch: Bringing Texture-Aware Colorization to Sketches
summary: Reference-based sketch colorization methods rely on large paired datasets that preserve both the structural and stylistic characteristics of hand-drawn artwork. However, existing datasets are limited in scale, expensive to annotate, and bound to fixed, often inconsistent artistic style biases that propagate to downstream models and limit cross-domain generalization. We present TexSketch, a controllable procedural framework for generating colored-sketch datasets with programmable artistic styles via geometric analysis and shader-driven stylization. Our fully automatic pipeline integrates region extraction, semantic color prediction, and shader-based rendering. By defining artistic appearance procedurally rather than inheriting it from a static corpus, TexSketch enables scalable dataset generation without manual annotation or artist supervision. Human studies demonstrate that TexSketch generates perceptually plausible colored sketches with high stylistic diversity, providing a controllable, scalable source of synthetic supervision for sketch colorization.

AI.tldr: TexSketch is a procedural framework for generating colored-sketch datasets with programmable artistic styles, enabling scalable dataset creation without manual annotation for reference-based sketch colorization.
AI.motivation: Existing datasets for reference-based sketch colorization are limited in scale, expensive to annotate, and bound to fixed artistic style biases that hinder cross-domain generalization.
AI.method: A fully automatic pipeline integrating region extraction, semantic color prediction, and shader-based rendering, with artistic appearance defined procedurally via geometric analysis and shader-driven stylization.
AI.result: The framework generates perceptually plausible colored sketches with high stylistic diversity, validated through human studies.
AI.conclusion: TexSketch provides a controllable, scalable source of synthetic supervision for sketch colorization, overcoming limitations of existing static, annotated datasets.

title: Mind the Microphone Gap: Benchmarking Array Upsampling Strategies for Latent Acoustic Mapping
summary: Latent Acoustic Mapping (LAM) is a self-supervised learning method that generates high-resolution spherical acoustic maps from multichannel recordings without labelled data, matching supervised baselines on direction-of-arrival benchmarks. However, LAM degrades significantly with sparse 4-channel arrays, as the low-resolution cross-spectral matrix captures far less spatial information than the 32-channel inputs LAM was designed for. We benchmark a diverse set of upsampling architectures, spanning lightweight convolutional networks, iterative back-projection models, physics-informed networks, and generative adversarial approaches. We also study whether aligning these upsamplers with LAM by training them jointly or in different stages helps preserve the spatial structure that LAM depends on. Results show that the original full-resolution LAM is the strongest, that separately trained lightweight models are the most competitive learned approaches, and that representation alignment between the upsampler and LAM matters more than model complexity.

AI.tldr: Benchmarks of various upsampling architectures to improve LAM's performance with sparse 4-channel arrays; finds separately trained lightweight models most effective, and representation alignment between upsampler and LAM more important than model complexity.
AI.motivation: LAM degrades significantly with sparse 4-channel arrays because the low-resolution cross-spectral matrix captures far less spatial information than the 32-channel inputs LAM was designed for.
AI.method: Benchmarked diverse upsampling architectures (lightweight convolutional networks, iterative back-projection models, physics-informed networks, generative adversarial approaches) and studied alignment strategies (joint training, staged training) between upsamplers and LAM.
AI.result: Original full-resolution LAM is strongest; separately trained lightweight models are most competitive among learned approaches; representation alignment between upsampler and LAM matters more than model complexity.
AI.conclusion: For improving LAM with sparse arrays, prioritize representation alignment and lightweight designs over complex upsampling architectures.

title: RMS@CC-MMD 2026: Multimodal Misogyny Detection via Geometric Interaction and Multi-View Consensus
comment: Accepted for the CC-MMD Grand Challenge at the 28th ACM International Conference on Multimodal Interaction (ICMI 2026)
summary: The proliferation of internet memes has introduced new complexities to automated content moderation, particularly in detecting misogyny. Memes often rely on a semantic clash between visual and textual modalities, where hateful intent is implicit and culturally grounded. This paper presents GeoMVC (Geometric Interaction and Multi-View Consensus), developed for the CC-MMD Grand Challenge at ICMI 2026. To address the limitations of static feature concatenation, a Geometric Interaction Layer is proposed that models cross-modal alignment via Hadamard products and cosine similarity between frozen visual and textual embeddings. We further mitigate distribution shifts caused by noisy OCR and code-mixed transliteration through a Multi-View Consensus strategy, aggregating predictions across raw, length-filtered, and English-translated text views. The system achieved Rank 2 in the Malayalam partition (Macro F1: 0.892) and Rank 3 in the Chinese partition (Macro F1: 0.895) on Task A, while securing Rank 5 in the Tamil partition (Macro F1: 0.521). A detailed error analysis on the development partition highlights open challenges in modeling localized transliteration and code-mixed sarcasm across Dravidian and Chinese cultural contexts.

AI.tldr: GeoMVC uses geometric cross-modal interaction and multi-view consensus to detect misogyny in internet memes, achieving top rankings across Malayalam, Chinese, and Tamil partitions at the CC-MMD Grand Challenge.
AI.motivation: Internet memes introduce complexities for automated content moderation due to implicit, culturally-grounded hateful intent arising from semantic clashes between visual and textual modalities; static feature concatenation fails to capture this cross-modal alignment.
AI.method: GeoMVC proposes a Geometric Interaction Layer using Hadamard products and cosine similarity between frozen visual and textual embeddings for cross-modal alignment, and a Multi-View Consensus strategy aggregating predictions across raw, length-filtered, and English-translated text views to handle noisy OCR and code-mixed transliteration.
AI.result: Rank 2 in Malayalam (Macro F1: 0.892), Rank 3 in Chinese (Macro F1: 0.895), Rank 5 in Tamil (Macro F1: 0.521) on Task A of the CC-MMD Grand Challenge.
AI.conclusion: Error analysis reveals open challenges in modeling localized transliteration and code-mixed sarcasm in Dravidian and Chinese cultural contexts, indicating room for improvement in culturally nuanced multimodal misogyny detection.

title: DomainPilot: Domain-Level Loss-Guided Two-Stage Data Mixture Optimization for Efficient Language Model Fine-Tuning
summary:
The training efficacy of large language models (LLMs) is fundamentally constrained by the quality and composition of training data. Existing dynamic data scheduling methods face critical limitations in industrial-scale pretraining and supervised fine-tuning (SFT): data selection incurs prohibitive O(N) costs on terabyte-scale corpora, mixture optimization schemes introduce severe I/O bottlenecks or require training auxiliary reference models, and sample-level reweighting strategies rely on loss signals that conflate noise, difficulty, and novelty.
  We present DomainPilot, a domain-level loss-guided two-stage data mixture optimization framework. DomainPilot introduces token-level domain loss monitoring to capture per-domain learning dynamics during training without halting the data pipeline. Building on these signals, we propose a Scaling Law guided coarse optimization stage that fits domain-specific convergence curves and derives a principled prior for mixture adjustment. A subsequent Mixing Law guided fine optimization stage refines the mixture by modeling cross-domain interaction effects through controlled sweep experiments. The entire mechanism is realized via a patch-based architecture that injects domain-aware loss computation into existing training frameworks (e.g., MindSpeed/Megatron-LM) with only ~30 lines of framework-specific adapter code.
  We validate DomainPilot on the Qwen3-1.7B model during SFT. Compared to the original data mixture, our optimized mixture achieves improvements of +2% on MMLU-Redux, +1.8% on AIME24, +3.8% on LiveCodeBench v5, and +3.6% on BFCL v3, without increasing total data volume or training cost. These results demonstrate that domain-level training signals provide an effective, lightweight alternative to expensive data selection or auxiliary model training for mixture optimization.

AI.tldr: DomainPilot is a domain-level loss-guided two-stage data mixture optimization framework for LLM training that uses token-level domain loss monitoring, Scaling Law guided coarse optimization, and Mixing Law guided fine optimization to improve data mixtures without increasing data volume or training cost, achieving +2% to +3.8% improvements on multiple benchmarks for Qwen3-1.7B SFT.
AI.motivation: Existing dynamic data scheduling methods (data selection, mixture optimization, sample-level reweighting) face prohibitive O(N) costs, severe I/O bottlenecks, require auxiliary reference models, or rely on loss signals that conflate noise, difficulty, and novelty—making them impractical for industrial-scale pretraining and SFT.
AI.method: DomainPilot employs (1) token-level domain loss monitoring to capture per-domain learning dynamics without halting the data pipeline; (2) Scaling Law guided coarse optimization to fit domain-specific convergence curves for principled prior mixture adjustment; (3) Mixing Law guided fine optimization to model cross-domain interaction effects via controlled sweep experiments; all realized through a patch-based architecture (~30 lines of adapter code) compatible with MindSpeed/Megatron-LM.
AI.result: On Qwen3-1.7B SFT, DomainPilot achieves +2% on MMLU-Redux, +1.8% on AIME24, +3.8% on LiveCodeBench v5, and +3.6% on BFCL v3 without increasing total data volume or training cost.
AI.conclusion: Domain-level training signals provide an effective, lightweight alternative to expensive data selection or auxiliary model training for mixture optimization.

title: Loss-Aware Feature-Map Pruning in Convolutional Neural Networks Using Multi-Armed Bandits
summary: Convolutional neural networks often contain redundant feature maps that increase storage and inference cost. This paper presents a loss-aware feature-map pruning framework using multi-armed bandits. Feature-map pruning is structured because it removes complete convolutional output channels and their producing filters rather than isolated scalar weights. Each candidate feature map is treated as an arm. At each play time, one map is temporarily masked and evaluated on a sampled mini-batch; the map is then restored and the observed loss change is converted into a safe-removal reward. After a fixed play budget, candidate maps are ranked by learned scores and the top-k maps are permanently removed with their filters, biases and corresponding next-layer input-channel kernels. The study evaluates UCB1 and Thompson Sampling, compares them with direct/oracle-style evaluation on LeNet/MNIST, and extends the evaluation to MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN, CUB-200-2011 and Oxford Flowers 102. Results show that UCB1 and Thompson Sampling preserve accuracy close to unpruned models while removing feature maps and reducing convolutional computation. Friedman and Nemenyi tests show that UCB1 obtains the highest mean rank, followed by Thompson Sampling; both significantly outperform greedy and magnitude-based pruning while remaining statistically comparable to the original unpruned model.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a loss-aware feature-map pruning framework for CNNs using multi-armed bandits (UCB1 and Thompson Sampling) to identify and remove redundant feature maps, achieving accuracy close to unpruned models while reducing computational cost.
AI.motivation: CNNs contain redundant feature maps that increase storage and inference cost; existing pruning methods often lack structured removal and awareness of loss impact.
AI.method: Each candidate feature map is treated as an arm in a multi-armed bandit; during a play budget, maps are temporarily masked, evaluated on mini-batches, and loss changes are converted into safe-removal rewards. After budget exhaustion, top-k maps are permanently removed along with their filters, biases, and corresponding next-layer input-channel kernels. UCB1 and Thompson Sampling are used as bandit algorithms.
AI.result: UCB1 and Thompson Sampling preserve accuracy close to unpruned models on MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN, CUB-200-2011, and Oxford Flowers 102. Friedman and Nemenyi tests show UCB1 achieves the highest mean rank, followed by Thompson Sampling; both significantly outperform greedy and magnitude-based pruning and are statistically comparable to the original unpruned model.
AI.conclusion: Multi-armed bandit-based feature-map pruning is an effective structured pruning approach that balances loss awareness and computational efficiency without sacrificing model accuracy.

title: LinkRank: A Learning-to-Rank Framework for One-to-Many Issue-Commit Traceability
summary: Recovering traceability links between issues and commits is important for software maintenance, debugging, impact analysis, and project understanding. However, most existing approaches assume a one-to-one relationship, where each issue is linked to a single commit. In practice, many issues are resolved through multiple commits, and ignoring this one-to-many nature can lead to incomplete traceability. This paper presents LinkRank, a learning-to-rank framework for recovering one-to-many issue--commit links. Unlike existing methods that mainly judge issue--commit pairs independently, LinkRank considers the set of candidate commits for an issue and identifies the commits that are most likely to contribute to its resolution. To support realistic evaluation, we construct a new dataset from six open-source GitHub repositories. LinkRank follows an iterative pick--remove--renormalize strategy: it selects the highest-ranked commit, removes it from the candidate pool, renormalizes the remaining scores, and repeats the process until the stopping criterion is met. We evaluate LinkRank under two settings: Known-K, where the true number of linked commits is available, and Unknown-K, where the model must infer when to stop selecting commits using ABS and REL stopping rules. Across six projects, LinkRank achieves an average Known-K F1 score of 74.54%, compared with 48.39% for the strongest baseline. In the Unknown-K setting, LinkRank achieves 68.84% F1 with ABS and 67.02% F1 with REL, outperforming the strongest baselines under both automatic stopping rules. Overall, the findings suggest that one-to-many issue--commit traceability is better addressed as an issue-centric ranking and iterative selection problem than as independent pairwise classification.

AI.tldr: LinkRank is a learning-to-rank framework for recovering one-to-many traceability links between issues and commits, which iteratively selects candidate commits per issue using a pick-remove-renormalize strategy, achieving F1 scores of 74.54% (Known-K) and 68.84%/67.02% (Unknown-K) across six GitHub projects, significantly outperforming baselines.
AI.motivation: Existing traceability recovery approaches assume a one-to-one relationship between issues and commits, but in practice many issues are resolved through multiple commits, leading to incomplete traceability links.
AI.method: LinkRank employs a learning-to-rank framework with an iterative pick-remove-renormalize strategy: it ranks candidate commits per issue, selects the highest-ranked commit, removes it from the pool, renormalizes remaining scores, and repeats until a stopping criterion is met. It supports both Known-K (true number of commits known) and Unknown-K (using ABS or REL stopping rules) settings.
AI.result: Across six open-source projects, LinkRank achieves 74.54% average F1 (Known-K) vs. 48.39% for the best baseline. In Unknown-K, it achieves 68.84% (ABS) and 67.02% (REL) F1, outperforming all baselines under both automatic stopping rules.
AI.conclusion: One-to-many issue-commit traceability is better formulated as an issue-centric ranking and iterative selection problem rather than independent pairwise classification.

title: A Smooth Explicit Elastoplastic--Damage Update for Graphics Simulation
summary:
History-dependent solids require material updates that preserve irreversible deformation and progressive degradation during loading, unloading, and reloading. We present a compact, vectorizable elastoplastic-damage update for explicit graphics simulation, designed for smooth activation and closed-form evaluation rather than exact yield-surface enforcement. A softplus function generates a candidate equivalent plastic strain, a maximum-history projection enforces irreversibility, and a deviatoric plastic-strain tensor retains the residual direction. An exponential scalar degradation variable is driven by the stored history. The active and frozen branches are evaluated analytically from one response energy without a local Newton solve.
  We evaluate the method using one-dimensional cyclic tension, two-dimensional cantilever bending, controlled three-dimensional platen compression, and a genus-one torus. The results verify residual deformation, monotone internal variables, branchwise energy-gradient agreement, and mesh-resolution sensitivity. An analytical J2 radial-return baseline is compared both as a vectorized kernel and within the same structural solver. The baseline is 1.51--3.08 times faster as a kernel and 1.69 times faster in the structural material update, showing that our contribution is smoothness and implementation simplicity rather than raw speed. A path-direction sweep gives 1.53% normalized equivalent-stress error under proportional loading but 49.39% for a fixed-magnitude 90-degree turn. This quantifies the method's intended restriction to isotropic, proportional or nearly proportional loading; it is not a replacement for general return mapping, anisotropic damage, or phase-field fracture.

AI.tldr: A compact, vectorizable elastoplastic-damage material update for explicit graphics simulation uses softplus activation, maximum-history projection, and closed-form evaluation without Newton solves, achieving smoothness and simplicity at the cost of accuracy under non-proportional loading.
AI.motivation: To provide a smooth, vectorizable, and analytically closed-form elastoplastic-damage update for explicit graphics simulation that avoids costly Newton iterations and complex yield-surface enforcement, prioritizing implementation simplicity and smooth activation over exact rheology.
AI.method: Softplus function for candidate equivalent plastic strain, maximum-history projection for irreversibility, deviatoric plastic-strain tensor for residual direction, exponential scalar degradation driven by stored history; all branches evaluated analytically from one response energy without local Newton solve.
AI.result: Validates residual deformation, monotone internal variables, energy-gradient agreement, and mesh sensitivity. Compared to J2 radial-return baseline, the method is 1.51-3.08× slower as kernel and 1.69× slower in structural update. Under proportional loading gives 1.53% normalized equivalent-stress error; under 90° turn gives 49.39% error.
AI.conclusion: The contribution is smoothness and simplicity, not speed; the method is restricted to isotropic, proportional/nearly proportional loading and is not a replacement for general return mapping, anisotropic damage, or phase-field fracture.

title: StanceBench: A Benchmark for Audio LLM-Based Interpersonal Stance Evaluation from Speech
summary: Speech-to-speech dialogue models increasingly depend on prosody and interactional nuance to convey social intent, yet benchmarks for these cues remain limited. We introduce StanceBench, a benchmark for measuring interpersonal stance in conversational speech and evaluating audio-capable LLMs as automated judges. Using the Seamless Interaction corpus, StanceBench (1) specifies 9 stance dimensions via role-prompt poles, (2) standardizes single-speaker and interaction-based evaluations, and (3) reports LLM-as-a-judge robustness, bias, and stance inference. Across evaluated stances, empathy and politeness are the easiest. Warmth and assertiveness are moderately separable with positivity skew/asymmetry. Honesty is the hardest and shows high prompt order bias, consistent with needing cross-turn evidence. Attentiveness is separable but aligns weakly with humans. Interaction stances are more context-sensitive, with threshold gaps and high variance, especially conflict regulation.

AI.tldr: StanceBench benchmarks interpersonal stance detection in conversational speech using 9 dimensions, evaluating LLMs as judges; empathy/politeness are easiest, honesty hardest, and interaction stances show high context-sensitivity.
AI.motivation: Speech-to-speech dialogue models increasingly rely on prosody and interactional nuance for social intent, but existing benchmarks for these cues are limited.
AI.method: StanceBench uses the Seamless Interaction corpus, defines 9 stance dimensions via role-prompt poles, standardizes single-speaker and interaction-based evaluations, and reports LLM-as-a-judge robustness, bias, and stance inference metrics.
AI.result: Empathy and politeness are easiest; warmth and assertiveness show positivity skew; honesty is hardest with high prompt order bias; attentiveness aligns weakly with humans; interaction stances show high variance, especially conflict regulation.
AI.conclusion: StanceBench highlights varying difficulty and bias patterns across stance dimensions, emphasizing the need for context-sensitive evaluation in conversational AI.

title: scMIR: a vision-language foundation model for single-cell light microscopy image representation
summary: Single-cell light microscopy images have become an important data source for characterizing cell phenotypes, but their complexity and heterogeneity pose challenges to high-throughput automated analysis. Existing representation learning methods mostly rely on task-oriented modeling, which is limited by specific datasets and predefined tasks, making them difficult to generalize across different cell types and microscopy modalities, and experimental conditions. Although general-purpose methods have improved the generalization ability of image representation in recent years, their limited utilization of experimental background and biological context information still poses challenges in complex phenotypic analysis. Here, we propose scMIR, a vision-language foundation model for single-cell light microscopy image representation. By synergistically combining self-supervised image reconstruction with text-guided cross-modal alignment, scMIR can simultaneously encode morphological and biological semantic information in a unified representation space. scMIR is pre-trained on 207,957 image-text pairs, covering various cell types, microscopy modalities, and perturbation conditions. scMIR outperforms existing general models and task-oriented methods as systematically evaluated on various complex tasks using 16 benchmark datasets, including cell classification, clustering, phenotype inference, and batch effect correction tasks. Furthermore, scMIR shows a strong generalization ability across various tasks without requiring task-specific fine-tuning. With its unique advantages, we envision scMIR may promote the standardization and automation of high-throughput phenotyping workflows through supporting various downstream analysis tasks.

AI.tldr: scMIR is a vision-language foundation model pre-trained on 207,957 image-text pairs that jointly learns morphology and biological semantics via self-supervised image reconstruction and text-guided cross-modal alignment, outperforming existing models across 16 benchmark datasets on cell classification, clustering, phenotype inference, and batch effect correction without task-specific fine-tuning.
AI.motivation: Existing representation learning methods for single-cell microscopy images either rely on task-specific modeling (limited generalization) or general-purpose approaches (poor utilization of biological context), hindering high-throughput automated phenotypic analysis across diverse cell types, modalities, and experimental conditions.
AI.method: scMIR synergistically combines self-supervised image reconstruction with text-guided cross-modal alignment to encode both morphological and biological semantic information in a unified representation space. It is pre-trained on 207,957 image-text pairs covering diverse cell types, microscopy modalities, and perturbation conditions.
AI.result: scMIR outperforms both general models and task-oriented methods across 16 benchmark datasets on cell classification, clustering, phenotype inference, and batch effect correction tasks, demonstrating strong zero-shot generalization without task-specific fine-tuning.
AI.conclusion: scMIR may promote the standardization and automation of high-throughput phenotyping workflows by supporting diverse downstream analysis tasks with a single unified representation.

title: Dementia Etiology Diagnosis via Collaborative Meta Knowledge Enhancement
summary: Although artificial intelligence (AI) has shown promising performance in several medical tasks, accurate dementia etiology diagnosis with AI remains challenging due to complex overlapping symptoms among diseases. Scaling up the dataset size by combining the cross-center samples may bring a gain in the pursuit of performance, while the inherent data heterogeneity across centers or populations induces the conflict. Conventional multi-task learning paradigms offer a promising framework; however, they fail to consider critical meta information (e.g., site-specific acquisition and modality availability) to combat the heterogeneity. To address this challenge, we propose a Collaborative Meta Knowledge Enhancement (COME) framework for dementia etiology diagnosis, which injects multi-center acquisition semantics, source identifiers, and modality indicators as heterogeneity-aware embeddings into a unified Transformer architecture for scale-up training, enabling explicit modeling of heterogeneity. Besides, a trust-region constrained optimization scheme is designed to regularize the model from spurious correlations during training through a reference model. Across seven independent cohorts, our method achieves state-of-the-art in-domain performance with a mean macro-averaged AUC of 85.62% and a 4.29-point gain over the strongest baseline, while maintaining superior out-of-domain generalization under both cross-center and cross-sequence evaluations. Extensive validation also confirms the alignment between model predictions and established biomarkers (amyloid, tau) and clinical severity, highlighting the potential of COME to enable robust and interpretable dementia diagnostics in real-world settings.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes COME, a Collaborative Meta Knowledge Enhancement framework for dementia etiology diagnosis that injects heterogeneity-aware embeddings (site-specific acquisition, source identifiers, modality indicators) into a unified Transformer architecture and uses trust-region constrained optimization to handle cross-center data heterogeneity, achieving state-of-the-art performance (85.62% mean macro-averaged AUC) across seven cohorts with strong generalization.
AI.motivation: Accurate dementia etiology diagnosis with AI is challenging due to complex overlapping symptoms. While cross-center data aggregation can improve performance, inherent data heterogeneity across centers/populations creates conflicts, and existing multi-task learning paradigms fail to incorporate critical meta information (site-specific acquisition, modality availability) to address this heterogeneity.
AI.method: The COME framework injects multi-center acquisition semantics, source identifiers, and modality indicators as heterogeneity-aware embeddings into a unified Transformer architecture. A trust-region constrained optimization scheme regularizes the model against spurious correlations during training via a reference model.
AI.result: Achieves state-of-the-art in-domain performance with 85.62% mean macro-averaged AUC and a 4.29-point gain over the strongest baseline across seven independent cohorts. Maintains superior out-of-domain generalization under cross-center and cross-sequence evaluations, with predictions aligning with established biomarkers (amyloid, tau) and clinical severity.
AI.conclusion: COME enables robust and interpretable dementia diagnostics in real-world settings by explicitly modeling heterogeneity and regularizing against spurious correlations, demonstrating potential for scalable cross-center AI deployment.

title: DSTFView: Multi-View Cloud-Edge Workload Forecasting with Dual-Input Spatio-Temporal-Frequency Modeling
summary: With the widespread deployment of edge-side AI inference, edge platforms are increasingly required to support latency-sensitive, highly concurrent, and reliability-critical applications. However, existing methods often struggle to balance multidimensional feature modeling and forecasting efficiency in collaborative cloud-edge environments. To address this issue, we propose DSTFView, a dual-input spatio-temporal-frequency multi-view workload forecasting framework for collaborative cloud-edge environments. It jointly models closeness and period dependencies and extracts spatial, temporal, and frequency-domain dependencies. Besides, it designs an adaptive fusion mechanism and adjusts the contribution of each view to capture abrupt changes. Experimental results on the CPU and TP datasets demonstrate that DSTFView consistently outperforms representative baselines across multiple forecasting horizons and evaluation metrics.

AI.tldr: DSTFView is a dual-input spatio-temporal-frequency multi-view workload forecasting framework for collaborative cloud-edge environments that jointly models closeness/period dependencies and spatial/temporal/frequency-domain features with an adaptive fusion mechanism, outperforming baselines on CPU and TP datasets.
AI.motivation: Existing methods struggle to balance multidimensional feature modeling and forecasting efficiency in collaborative cloud-edge environments, which need to support latency-sensitive, highly concurrent, and reliability-critical applications.
AI.method: Proposes DSTFView, a dual-input spatio-temporal-frequency multi-view workload forecasting framework that: (1) jointly models closeness and period dependencies, (2) extracts spatial, temporal, and frequency-domain dependencies, and (3) designs an adaptive fusion mechanism to adjust each view's contribution for capturing abrupt changes.
AI.result: Consistently outperforms representative baselines across multiple forecasting horizons and evaluation metrics on both CPU and TP datasets.
AI.conclusion: DSTFView effectively addresses the challenge of balancing multidimensional feature modeling and forecasting efficiency in collaborative cloud-edge environments through its multi-view adaptive fusion approach.

title: Where Is the Cost of Third-Party API Routers in Agentic Software Development?
summary: Third-party API routers have become a common layer that unifies access across increasingly diverse LLM providers. In coding-agent workflows, high-autonomy operation is widely adopted because it reduces interaction overhead. As a result, a third-party API router, which sits between the agent and the upstream provider, inevitably occupies the trusted path. It can inspect and modify every request and response, yet no mechanism verifies alignment between the provider's output and the repository-level actions ultimately executed by the agent. Consequently, client-side permission mechanisms may become ineffective in practice. Whether this control gap produces real, hard-to-detect effects on software development tasks remains empirically unmeasured. In this paper, we conduct an empirical study of router-side injection in coding agents, examining four intervention levels of increasing subtlety: Response Substitution (L1), Response Append (L2), LLM-Polished Injection (L3), and LLM-Polished with Distribution Alignment Injection (L4). Moreover, we develop SIDEL, a framework for trace recording, replay, injection, and defense evaluation, with a curated dataset of 400 samples. We evaluate four representative coding agents, and further evaluate whitelist-based execution control and LLM review. Router-side intervention substantially alters repository-level actions and remains difficult for existing client-side safeguards to detect. Without additional mitigations, all evaluated agents achieved a defense success rate of 0 percent across all injection levels. Client-side mitigations and reactive reviews improve resistance but do not fully restore end-to-end control, motivating provider-side output-integrity guarantees. Our code is available at https://github.com/Riyasushin/SIDE.

AI.tldr: This paper empirically studies router-side injection attacks in coding-agent workflows where third-party API routers sit on the trusted path between agents and LLM providers. The authors define four intervention levels (L1-L4) of increasing subtlety, develop the SIDEL framework with 400 samples, and evaluate four coding agents. Results show router-side intervention substantially alters repository-level actions, with all agents achieving 0% defense success rate without mitigations. Client-side safeguards (whitelist-based execution control, LLM review) improve resistance but cannot fully restore end-to-end control.
AI.motivation: Third-party API routers occupy the trusted path in coding-agent workflows, enabling them to inspect and modify requests/responses without any mechanism to verify alignment between provider outputs and executed repository-level actions. This creates a control gap that may render client-side permission mechanisms ineffective, yet the empirical effects on software development tasks remain unmeasured.
AI.method: The authors conduct an empirical study defining four intervention levels of increasing subtlety: Response Substitution (L1), Response Append (L2), LLM-Polished Injection (L3), and LLM-Polished with Distribution Alignment Injection (L4). They develop SIDEL, a framework for trace recording, replay, injection, and defense evaluation, using a curated dataset of 400 samples. They evaluate four representative coding agents and test whitelist-based execution control and LLM review as defenses.
AI.result: Router-side intervention substantially alters repository-level actions and is difficult for existing client-side safeguards to detect. All evaluated agents achieved 0% defense success rate across all injection levels without additional mitigations. Client-side mitigations and reactive reviews improve resistance but do not fully restore end-to-end control.
AI.conclusion: The control gap introduced by third-party API routers in coding-agent workflows poses a real and hard-to-detect security threat. Current client-side defenses are insufficient, motivating the need for provider-side output-integrity guarantees to ensure end-to-end control.

title: Coherent Visualization of 2D Scalar Field Contour Ensembles With Probabilistic Latent Space Modeling
comment: Accepted by IEEE VIS 2026. To appear in IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics
summary: We present a new visualization method for contour ensembles through probabilistic modeling. We aim to improve the coherence between different visual representations, such as contour boxplots and density plots for a 2D scalar field ensemble. We model each ensemble member with a probabilistic representation in the latent space, i.e., a lower-dimensional representation of spatial data features, of a variational autoencoder (VAE). Thereafter, efficient data depth computation and uncertainty-aware clustering are supported based on a matrix of pair-wise similarity measurements of members. We estimate the underlying probability distribution by leveraging the power of VAE to create density plots that align more coherently with member distributions than existing methods. The effectiveness of our method is evaluated through numerical comparisons with existing techniques, and visualization examples of synthetic and real-world ensemble datasets.

AI.tldr: A new VAE-based probabilistic modeling method for contour ensemble visualization that improves coherence between contour boxplots and density plots by computing data depth and uncertainty-aware clustering in latent space.
AI.motivation: To improve the coherence between different visual representations (e.g., contour boxplots and density plots) for 2D scalar field ensembles, addressing alignment issues in existing methods.
AI.method: Each ensemble member is modeled with a probabilistic representation in the latent space of a variational autoencoder (VAE). Pair-wise similarity measurements are computed for efficient data depth and uncertainty-aware clustering. Density plots are generated from the learned probability distribution.
AI.result: Numerical comparisons show the method outperforms existing techniques; demonstrated via synthetic and real-world ensemble datasets.
AI.conclusion: VAE-based latent space probabilistic modeling enables more coherent contour boxplots and density plots for ensemble visualization, with effectiveness validated both quantitatively and qualitatively.

title: Multimodal Domain Generalization for Depression Detection: An Attention-Based BiLSTM Network with Domain-Adversarial Training
comment: 12 pages, 8 figures, 6 tables. Accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems (TNNLS)
summary: Automatic depression detection with deep learning has shown promise but often suffers from limited generalization due to domain shift arising from inter-speaker variability. To address this critical issue, we present the first patient-independent multimodal depression detection framework that incorporates domain generalization (DG), jointly leveraging both acoustic and textual modalities. The proposed model integrates bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) with intra- and cross-modal attention mechanisms, accompanied by segment-level fusion for decision-making. Generalization is further enhanced by applying a gradient reversal layer inspired by Domain-Adversarial Training of Neural Networks (DANN), which promotes domain-invariant representations by adversarially limiting the model's ability to identify individual speakers, effectively reducing patient-specific bias. Conducting experiments on the Androids-Corpus dataset with a 5-fold cross-validation (CV) protocol, various pairings of audio and text feature extractors were evaluated over different segment durations, determining MelSpec and ItalianBERT as the optimal baseline at a 30-second segment duration. The addition of DG to this baseline yields a 2.5% increase in accuracy and 3.3% in F1-score, achieving 93.2% accuracy, 93.2% precision, 96.2% recall, and 94.2% F1-score, surpassing all existing benchmarks. Extensive ablation studies assess the impact of multimodal fusion, deep architectural choices, and DG, highlighting their combined contribution to robust and generalizable depression detection.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first patient-independent multimodal (audio+text) depression detection framework using domain generalization with a DANN-inspired gradient reversal layer to reduce inter-speaker bias, achieving 93.2% accuracy and 94.2% F1-score on the Androids-Corpus dataset, surpassing all existing benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Automatic depression detection with deep learning suffers from limited generalization due to domain shift caused by inter-speaker variability. The authors aim to address this by proposing a patient-independent framework that reduces patient-specific bias.
AI.method: A multimodal framework integrating BiLSTM with intra- and cross-modal attention mechanisms and segment-level fusion, enhanced by a gradient reversal layer (inspired by DANN) that adversarially limits the model's ability to identify individual speakers, promoting domain-invariant representations.
AI.result: With MelSpec and ItalianBERT as optimal baselines at 30-second segments, adding DG yields 2.5% accuracy improvement and 3.3% F1-score increase, achieving 93.2% accuracy, 93.2% precision, 96.2% recall, and 94.2% F1-score, surpassing all existing benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: The combined contributions of multimodal fusion, deep architectural choices, and domain generalization are essential for robust and generalizable depression detection, with extensive ablation studies confirming their effectiveness.

title: Real-Time Semantic Segmentation with Optimized RetinaNet Architectures for Embedded Automotive Systems
summary: Real-time perception is a foundational requirement for advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and autonomous vehicles, yet embedded automotive platforms impose severe constraints on compute, memory, and power. This paper presents an optimized semantic segmentation architecture derived from the RetinaNet detection framework, adapted for dense pixel-wise prediction and tailored for deployment on resource-constrained embedded hardware. The proposed architecture, termed Opt-RetinaSeg, replaces the standard ResNet-50 backbone with a hybrid lightweight feature extractor, restructures the Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) to reduce redundant multi-scale computation, and introduces a compact segmentation head guided by focal-loss-inspired class balancing to address the severe foreground-background imbalance common in road scenes. We further apply a three-stage optimization pipeline consisting of structured channel pruning, post-training INT8 quantization, and knowledge distillation from a high-capacity teacher network. Evaluated on the Cityscapes and BDD100K datasets and deployed on an NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX and a Qualcomm QCS610 automotive SoC, the proposed model achieves 73.9% mIoU at 70.4 FPS, representing a 7.4x inference speedup and a 4x reduction in model size relative to the ResNet-50 baseline, with less than 3% accuracy degradation. These results indicate that RetinaNet-derived architectures, when systematically optimized, are viable candidates for real-time semantic segmentation in embedded automotive perception pipelines

AI.tldr: The paper presents Opt-RetinaSeg, a semantic segmentation architecture adapted from RetinaNet for embedded automotive platforms. It uses a lightweight backbone, restructured FPN, and focal-loss-inspired segmentation head, optimized via channel pruning, INT8 quantization, and knowledge distillation, achieving 73.9% mIoU at 70.4 FPS on NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX and Qualcomm QCS610 with 7.4x speedup and 4x size reduction over ResNet-50 baseline.
AI.motivation: Real-time perception for ADAS and autonomous vehicles faces severe compute, memory, and power constraints on embedded automotive platforms, necessitating efficient semantic segmentation architectures.
AI.method: Opt-RetinaSeg adapts RetinaNet for dense pixel-wise prediction by: (1) replacing ResNet-50 with a hybrid lightweight feature extractor, (2) restructuring FPN to reduce redundant multi-scale computation, (3) introducing a compact segmentation head with focal-loss-inspired class balancing, and (4) applying a three-stage optimization pipeline: structured channel pruning, post-training INT8 quantization, and knowledge distillation from a high-capacity teacher.
AI.result: Achieved 73.9% mIoU at 70.4 FPS on Cityscapes and BDD100K datasets deployed on NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX and Qualcomm QCS610, with 7.4x inference speedup, 4x model size reduction, and less than 3% accuracy degradation relative to ResNet-50 baseline.
AI.conclusion: RetinaNet-derived architectures, when systematically optimized, are viable candidates for real-time semantic segmentation in embedded automotive perception pipelines.

title: CC-AOS: Cost- and Horizon-Conditioned Amortized Backward Induction for Finite-Horizon Optimal Stopping
summary: Finite-horizon optimal stopping is a central problem in early time-series classification, where a system must decide at each sequence prefix whether the expected benefit of another observation justifies its acquisition cost. Existing data-driven backward-induction methods typically solve each cost-horizon operating point separately, so changing operating conditions requires repeated optimization and separate model stacks, making continuous cost adaptation and multi-horizon deployment inefficient. We propose CC-AOS (Cost- and Horizon-Conditioned Amortized Optimal Stopping), a structured amortized solver for a family of finite-horizon stopping problems with continuous costs and multiple horizons. CC-AOS learns a shared continuation-value model conditioned on the current state, absolute time, remaining horizon, and acquisition cost through joint amortized fitted backward induction. We establish that the exact value and continuation functions are nondecreasing, concave, and horizon-dependently Lipschitz in cost, encode these properties in the model architecture, and derive residual-based bounds on value and policy errors. Experiments on controlled Gaussian and time-varying non-Gaussian processes and the FordA engine-noise time-series benchmark compare CC-AOS with representative per-operating-point backward-induction solvers and tuned static stopping rules. At six unseen FordA cost-horizon pairs, one CC-AOS checkpoint achieved a lower terminal-risk-plus-sampling-cost objective than independently fitted Convex Function Learning at all six pairs, with an average reduction of 15.75 percent, while matching the tuned static thresholds on average.

AI.tldr: CC-AOS is an amortized optimal stopping solver that handles continuous costs and multiple horizons via a shared continuation-value model with theoretical guarantees, outperforming independent per-operating-point solvers on benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing data-driven backward-induction methods solve each cost-horizon operating point separately, requiring repeated optimization and separate model stacks, which makes continuous cost adaptation and multi-horizon deployment inefficient.
AI.method: CC-AOS learns a shared continuation-value model conditioned on state, absolute time, remaining horizon, and acquisition cost through joint amortized fitted backward induction, with architectural encoding of theoretical properties (nondecreasing, concave, horizon-dependently Lipschitz in cost).
AI.result: On six unseen FordA cost-horizon pairs, one CC-AOS checkpoint achieved a 15.75% average reduction in objective (terminal risk plus sampling cost) over Convex Function Learning, while matching tuned static thresholds on average.
AI.conclusion: CC-AOS enables efficient multi-horizon, continuous-cost optimal stopping with strong theoretical guarantees and empirical performance, eliminating the need for per-operating-point re-optimization.

title: MedLoCoMo: A Long-Context Multi-Session Medical Dialogue Benchmark for Large Language Models
summary: MedLoCoMo is a Medical Long-Context Memory benchmark for patient-specific clinical reasoning over multi-admission medical dialogue. Existing medical QA benchmarks largely test short context knowledge or single document grounding, leaving open whether LLMs can use, connect, and abstain over longitudinal patient histories. We build MedLoCoMo from deidentified MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-IV-Note records by constructing admission-level clinical packets, synthesizing grounded doctor-patient conversations, and generating evidence linked QA items over single-admission, cross-admission, and adversarial unanswerable settings. The benchmark contains 100 patient timelines averaging 1,669.8 turns, 29.7 sessions, and 74,512.2 tokens per conversation. Across the evaluated baselines, cross-admission reasoning is consistently harder than localized evidence use, even when models have long context windows or use external memory or retrieval methods. The code and MedLoCoMo benchmark release is available at https://github.com/leozzy13/MedLoCoMo for use and reproducibility.

AI.tldr: MedLoCoMo is a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on patient-specific clinical reasoning across multi-admission medical dialogues, finding cross-admission reasoning harder than single-admission evidence use even with long-context or retrieval-augmented models.
AI.motivation: Existing medical QA benchmarks focus on short-context knowledge or single-document grounding, lacking evaluation of whether LLMs can use, connect, and abstain from reasoning over longitudinal patient histories spanning multiple admissions.
AI.method: Constructed from deidentified MIMIC-IV/MIMIC-IV-Note records by building admission-level clinical packets, synthesizing grounded doctor-patient conversations, and generating evidence-linked QA items across three settings: single-admission, cross-admission, and adversarial unanswerable. Contains 100 patient timelines averaging 1,669.8 turns, 29.7 sessions, and 74,512.2 tokens per conversation.
AI.result: Cross-admission reasoning consistently outperformed localized evidence use across all evaluated baselines, even when models had long context windows or used external memory/retrieval methods.
AI.conclusion: MedLoCoMo reveals a persistent gap in longitudinal clinical reasoning capabilities of current LLMs, highlighting the need for better long-context medical reasoning approaches.

title: Multi-level Code Optimization via Mixture of Prompts
comment: This paper has been accepted by ASE 2026
summary:
Runtime efficiency is a critical factor that impacts both software quality and user satisfaction. There are many approaches proposed for code optimization to improve runtime efficiency. Traditional code optimization methods operate on intermediate representations (IRs) during compilation for static languages. They are effective but struggle to handle dynamic languages that do not require compilation. Recently, large language models (LLMs) have been leveraged to directly optimize source code in dynamic languages.
