AI.tldr: SFPruner is a non-iterative, single-forward-pass visual token pruning framework that embeds redundancy control into the scoring space using semantics-guided ridge leverage and ranking-based directional masking, achieving up to 110ms selection speedup (112.4ms → 2.5ms at 512 tokens) while maintaining competitive performance under aggressive compression.
AI.motivation: Existing subset-optimization token pruning methods suffer from sequential dependency and iterative subset construction, causing high selection overhead that limits actual wall-clock speedups despite theoretical FLOPs reductions, especially as visual token counts scale up in high-resolution MLLMs.
AI.method: SFPruner reformulates visual token pruning structurally by (1) a semantics-guided ridge leverage scheme that attenuates redundancy at the covariance level by integrating instruction relevance and visual saliency to suppress dominant covariance directions, and (2) ranking-based directional masking that resolves residual overlap via asymmetric similarity competition, where higher-scoring tokens suppress redundant lower-scoring alternatives through parallel tensor operations—all in a single forward pass without iterative optimization.
AI.result: SFPruner reduces token selection time from 112.4ms to 2.5ms at 512 tokens (110ms improvement) on Qwen2.5-VL, demonstrating stable selection costs across scales and successfully translating theoretical token reductions into actual inference speedups while preserving competitive performance against state-of-the-art methods under aggressive compression.
AI.conclusion: The structural efficiency of non-iterative, single-forward-pass pruning effectively bridges the gap between theoretical FLOPs reductions and practical wall-clock speedups, offering a scalable solution for visual token explosion in high-resolution MLLMs.

title: XGRVFL-MV: Residual-Coupled Graph-Embedded Multi-View Random Vector Functional Link Network with FleXi Guardian Loss
summary: Random Vector Functional Link (RVFL) networks provide an efficient randomized learning framework for classification. Existing multi-view RVFL methods utilize complementary information from multiple views. However, preserving view-specific geometric structure, limiting the influence of large prediction residuals, and modeling relationships between multiple views remain challenging. This paper proposes a Residual-Coupled Graph-Embedded Multi-View RVFL model with fleXi guardian loss (XGRVFL-MV) for multi-view classification. The proposed model constructs RVFL representation for each view, incorporates graph embedding with intrinsic and penalty graphs constructed using the Local Fisher Discriminant Analysis weighting scheme. It also uses the bounded and asymmetric FleXi Guardian (XG) loss for residual learning. A residual-coupling term is introduced to encourage consistency among view-specific prediction residuals while preserving view-specific representations. The resulting optimization problem is solved using an inversion-free first-order optimization procedure based on Nesterov accelerated gradient descent. We evaluate the proposed model on UCI, KEEL, AwA, and Corel5k benchmark datasets. Experimental results, together with statistical analyses and hyperparameter sensitivity analyses, show that XGRVFL-MV achieves competitive classification performance compared with the baseline methods across the evaluated benchmark datasets.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes XGRVFL-MV, a multi-view classification model that integrates graph embedding with Local Fisher Discriminant Analysis weighting, bounded asymmetric FleXi Guardian loss for residual learning, and a residual-coupling term for view consistency, solved via Nesterov accelerated gradient descent, achieving competitive performance on UCI, KEEL, AwA, and Corel5k datasets.
AI.motivation: Existing multi-view RVFL methods struggle with preserving view-specific geometric structure, limiting the influence of large prediction residuals, and modeling relationships between multiple views.
AI.method: The model constructs RVFL representations per view, incorporates graph embedding with intrinsic/penalty graphs via Local Fisher Discriminant Analysis weighting, uses bounded asymmetric FleXi Guardian (XG) loss for residual learning, and introduces a residual-coupling term for cross-view consistency. Optimization uses inversion-free Nesterov accelerated gradient descent.
AI.result: XGRVFL-MV achieves competitive classification performance compared to baseline methods across UCI, KEEL, AwA, and Corel5k benchmark datasets, supported by statistical and hyperparameter sensitivity analyses.
AI.conclusion: The proposed residual-coupled graph-embedded multi-view RVFL with XG loss effectively addresses geometric structure preservation, residual robustness, and multi-view relationship modeling for classification.

title: TRACE: Business Rule-Grounded Reasoning Curriculum for Knowledge-Preserving Parametric Tool Retrieval in Enterprise LLMs
summary: Parametric retrieval enables LLMs to retrieve tools implicitly by assigning each API a unique virtual token and training the model to generate it via constrained beam search. Toolsense shows that this regime has two critical drawbacks: it destroys parametric tool knowledge during training, and its beam-search decoding is too slow for real-time deployment. We introduce TRACE (Tool Retrieval via Augmented Chain-of-thought and Enterprise rules), a two-stage curriculum that resolves this dissociation. Stage 1 reuses the multi-format memorization SFT from ToolSense to seed tool knowledge with LoRA. Stage 2 is our core contribution: the model is trained to emit a thinking trace before producing a JSON list of tool tokens, using two data sources -- RRB pairs from ToolSense and queries synthesized to target business rules curated by domain experts -- both augmented with reasoning traces. This training objective preserves Stage 1 MCQ and QA probing accuracy while enabling single-beam greedy decoding at production latency. Evaluated on a combined enterprise catalog of 8,300+ tools across two enterprise product lines, TRACE training for Stage 2 not only preserves but improves tool understanding: MCQ accuracy gains +3.2 pp and QA probing gains +9 pp over Stage 1. On retrieval, TRACE achieves ~86% recall on Domain A and ~60% on Domain B -- compared to embedding baseline performance of ~27% & ~52% -- both with single-beam greedy decoding, making it directly deployable at production latency.

AI.tldr: TRACE is a two-stage curriculum training method that overcomes the dissociation problem in parametric tool retrieval for LLMs by adding a thinking trace before tool token generation. It preserves tool knowledge, enables single-beam greedy decoding (faster than constrained beam search), and improves retrieval recall significantly (86% on Domain A, 60% on Domain B) compared to embedding baselines (~27% and ~52%).
AI.motivation: Parametric retrieval (e.g., ToolSense) destroys parametric tool knowledge during training and suffers from slow beam-search decoding, making it unsuitable for real-time enterprise deployment.
AI.method: TRACE employs a two-stage curriculum: Stage 1 reuses multi-format memorization SFT from ToolSense with LoRA to seed tool knowledge; Stage 2 trains the model to emit a thinking trace before producing a JSON list of tool tokens, using RRB pairs and business-rule-targeted synthesized queries augmented with reasoning traces, then decodes via single-beam greedy search.
AI.result: Stage 2 preserves or improves Stage 1 performance: MCQ accuracy +3.2 pp, QA probing +9 pp. Retrieval recall reaches ~86% (Domain A) and ~60% (Domain B), drastically outperforming embedding baselines (~27% and ~52%). Achieves production-latency decoding via single-beam greedy search.
AI.conclusion: Adding a chain-of-thought thinking trace before tool token generation resolves the dissociation between parametric tool knowledge and retrieval, enabling accurate, fast, and deployable enterprise tool retrieval.

title: Similarity Is Not Logic: Factored Inference for Dual-Encoder Vision-Language Models
comment: Accepted at ICML 2026. 18 pages, 8 figures. Project page: https://sultanmo.github.io/factored-vlm Code and benchmark: https://github.com/SultanMo/factored-vlm
summary: Dual-encoder vision-language models (VLMs) expose a similarity interface that enables zero-shot retrieval but fails compositional constraints: queries like "umbrella and no person" retrieve images containing both, even when concept detection is reliable. We trace this to an interface-level Bag-of-Concepts effect, where similarity scores approximate mean pooling of concept evidence regardless of operators. Although operator-dependent signals exist in text embeddings, they are too weak or misaligned to affect rankings. Fine-tuning does not reliably resolve this failure because the dominant bottleneck is how similarity aggregates evidence rather than what encoders represent. We propose factored inference, which separates evidence extraction from constraint execution, and introduce LCSE (Logic-Constrained Score Editing), a training-free method that executes constraints externally using concept scores from frozen encoders. We also introduce FACTOR-Bench, where LCSE achieves 85.5% accuracy versus 73.2% for the best fine-tuned baseline, 90.7% when applied to SigLIP 2, and improves NegBench COCO MCQ accuracy from 27.2% to 65.2% while preserving retrieval performance.

AI.tldr: Dual-encoder VLMs fail compositional reasoning due to a Bag-of-Concepts effect where similarity scores average concept evidence irrespective of logical operators. The authors propose LCSE (Logic-Constrained Score Editing), a training-free method that separates evidence extraction from constraint execution, achieving 85.5% on FACTOR-Bench vs 73.2% for fine-tuned baselines.
AI.motivation: Dual-encoder VLMs fail compositional constraints (e.g., "umbrella and no person") due to a Bag-of-Concepts effect where similarity scores aggregate all concept evidence equally regardless of logical operators, and fine-tuning does not reliably fix this bottleneck.
AI.method: Proposes factored inference that separates evidence extraction from constraint execution, and introduces LCSE (Logic-Constrained Score Editing), a training-free method that externally executes logical constraints using concept scores from frozen encoders.
AI.result: LCSE achieves 85.5% on FACTOR-Bench vs 73.2% for best fine-tuned baseline; 90.7% when applied to SigLIP 2; improves NegBench COCO MCQ from 27.2% to 65.2% while preserving retrieval performance.
AI.conclusion: The similarity interface bottleneck in dual-encoder VLMs can be overcome by external constraint execution without fine-tuning, demonstrating that the dominant issue is how evidence is aggregated rather than what encoders represent.

title: In-Context Learning as Implicit Policy Gradient
summary: Recent work has shown that large language models (LLMs) can iteratively improve their outputs by incorporating generated samples and their corresponding evaluation scores as in-context examples. Despite these empirical findings, the theoretical foundations underlying this phenomenon remain poorly understood. In this paper, we show that score-conditioned In-Context Learning (ICL) admits a structural correspondence to policy gradient optimization. We first provide a constructive proof that self-attention mechanisms can implement reward-weighted aggregation analogous to the REINFORCE algorithm under specific weight matrix configurations, and discuss the relationship between this construction and the behavior of pretrained transformers. The correspondence is directional in hidden-state space and holds exactly only under the stated simplifying conditions; we quantify its strength empirically. Within our simplified hidden-state model, we furthermore derive an exact upper bound on the distribution shift induced by a bounded attention update, yielding a trust-region-like analogy to KL-constrained policy optimization. We validate our theory through extensive experiments across multiple LLMs, demonstrating that LLMs effectively utilize score information to shift output distributions toward high-scoring exemplars, and that attention weights exhibit a strong correlation with example scores.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a theoretical connection between score-conditioned In-Context Learning (ICL) in LLMs and policy gradient optimization, specifically the REINFORCE algorithm. It provides a constructive proof that self-attention can implement reward-weighted aggregation, derives an upper bound on distribution shift analogous to KL-constrained policy optimization, and validates findings through experiments showing LLMs effectively use score information to shift output distributions.
AI.motivation: Despite empirical evidence that LLMs can iteratively improve outputs by using generated samples and evaluation scores as in-context examples, the theoretical foundations underlying this score-conditioned ICL phenomenon remain poorly understood.
AI.method: The paper provides a constructive proof that self-attention mechanisms can implement reward-weighted aggregation (analogous to REINFORCE) under specific weight matrix configurations, derives an upper bound on distribution shift from bounded attention updates (trust-region analogy), and validates claims through extensive experiments across multiple LLMs.
AI.result: LLMs effectively utilize score information to shift output distributions toward high-scoring exemplars; attention weights exhibit strong correlation with example scores; the structural correspondence between score-conditioned ICL and policy gradient optimization holds directionally in hidden-state space under simplifying conditions.
AI.conclusion: Score-conditioned ICL structurally corresponds to policy gradient optimization (REINFORCE), with self-attention capable of implementing reward-weighted aggregation, and bounded attention updates produce distribution shifts analogous to KL-constrained trust-region policy optimization.

title: DishSeg24k: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Food Segmentation with Stochastic Expert Decoding
summary: Food segmentation is essential for applications such as intelligent catering, dietary assessment, and recommendation. However, existing benchmarks fail to capture the complexity of real-world dining scenes. The challenges of dense inter-dish overlap, fine-grained class similarity, and extreme long-tail class distributions exceed the fidelity of current datasets. To fill this gap, we introduce \textbf{DishSeg24k}, a large-scale dish-level segmentation benchmark with 24,096 images, 112,281 instances, and 278 fine-grained categories in real-world dining environments. Based on DishSeg24k, we further propose \textbf{Food Expert-Adaptive Segmentation Transformers (FEAST)} to address these challenges. FEAST models query-based decoding as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), where each decoder layer update is treated as a sequential decision step that explores uncertainty along dish boundaries. We further redesign the decoder with a reinforcement learning (RL)-guided Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) module, in which a dual-critic decoupled optimization scheme separates task-oriented query refinement from structure-aware expert routing. This design promotes expert specialization and prevents expert collapse under long-tail category distributions. Finally, extensive experiments on DishSeg24k demonstrate the state-of-the-art performance of FEAST, which outperforms previous methods by {+3.21\%} mIoU, {+3.68\%} mDice, and {+4.00\%} mAcc, respectively. We further validate the effectiveness of FEAST on FoodSeg103. The dataset and code will be publicly released.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces DishSeg24k, a large-scale dish-level segmentation benchmark with 24,096 images and 278 categories for real-world dining scenes, and proposes FEAST, a segmentation model using MDP-based query decoding and RL-guided Mixture-of-Experts with dual-critic optimization, achieving state-of-the-art performance.
AI.motivation: Existing food segmentation benchmarks fail to capture real-world dining complexity, including dense inter-dish overlap, fine-grained class similarity, and extreme long-tail class distributions.
AI.method: FEAST models query-based decoding as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), uses reinforcement learning (RL)-guided Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) module, and employs a dual-critic decoupled optimization scheme for task-oriented query refinement and structure-aware expert routing.
AI.result: FEAST outperforms previous methods by +3.21% mIoU, +3.68% mDice, and +4.00% mAcc on DishSeg24k, with further validation on FoodSeg103.
AI.conclusion: The proposed DishSeg24k benchmark and FEAST method address key limitations in food segmentation, establishing a new state-of-the-art and will be publicly released for future research.

title: Wrong Design Intent Is Worse Than None: A Derangement-Control Diagnosis of Header Conditioning in CAD Program Completion
summary: Fine-tuned code LLMs can be conditioned on a lightweight design-intent header to steer parametric CAD generation, but whether the model actually reads the header's content has not been tested under a metric independent of the conditioning itself, nor with a causal control. We study CADCON, a five-feature design-intent header prepended to CadQuery-style sketch-extrude programs during LoRA fine-tuning of Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B, re-scored by executable geometric assertions on the produced B-rep solid, sharing no code with the header-defining regex extractor. Across three seeds and a pre-registered {0%, 40%}-prefix $\times$ {correct, wrong, masked}-header matrix we find: (i) in conditional completion (40% prefix), a semantically wrong header degrades adherence below the no-header baseline (0.43 $\to$ 0.30/0.21 text/token) on design intents the model can render unconditioned -- polygonal and thin geometries; circle and tall intents sit at a baseline generation floor for this checkpoint ($\approx$0 in both compared arms) and are uninformative for this contrast; (ii) a derangement control -- retrained with shuffled ground-truth headers, identical header marginal but destroyed content correlation -- remains competent yet is immune to wrong headers, while the standard model is not (text headers; interaction significant on 3/3 seeds, p $\leq$ $4.2\times10^{-3}$): the harm requires the learned header$\to$program mapping, excluding the marginal/mechanical distribution-shift confound; (iii) the independent metric deflates the apparent benefit of a correct header (token: +0.21 regex $\to$ +0.02 geometry), quantifying metric circularity; (iv) the harm is regime-specific -- at 0% prefix the unconditioned baseline cannot generate valid CAD at all. Wrong intent is not noise: it actively misdirects generation.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether fine-tuned code LLMs genuinely read design-intent headers for parametric CAD generation. Using CADCON, a five-feature header prepended to CadQuery programs during LoRA fine-tuning of Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B, the authors evaluate via executable geometric assertions (independent metric). Key findings: (1) semantically wrong headers degrade performance below no-header baselines; (2) a derangement control (shuffled headers) is immune to wrong headers, proving harm requires learned header→program mapping; (3) the independent metric reveals inflated benefits of correct headers from metric circularity; (4) effects are regime-specific—no effect at 0% prefix where the model cannot generate valid CAD.
AI.motivation: To test whether code LLMs actually condition on design-intent headers during parametric CAD generation, using a metric independent of the conditioning and a causal control, since prior work has not established causal evidence that the model reads the header content.
AI.method: Fine-tuned Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B with LoRA on CadQuery-style sketch-extrude programs prepended with a CADCON header (five features: polygonal, thin, circle, tall, rect). Evaluated with executable geometric assertions on produced B-rep solids (independent metric). Used {0%, 40%} prefix × {correct, wrong, masked} header matrix across three seeds, plus a derangement control with shuffled ground-truth headers.
AI.result: Wrong headers degrade performance below no-header baselines (0.43→0.30/0.21 text/token) for polygonal and thin geometries. Derangement model is immune to wrong headers while standard model is harmed (significant on 3/3 seeds, p≤4.2×10^{-3}). Independent metric deflates correct-header benefit (token: +0.21 regex→+0.02 geometry). At 0% prefix, model cannot generate valid CAD at all.
AI.conclusion: The model genuinely reads and is causally affected by design-intent headers; wrong headers actively misdirect generation rather than acting as noise. Metric circularity inflates apparent benefits. Effects depend on the model's baseline competence for specific design intents.

title: Reason Before You Retrieve: Agentic Planning for Multi-modal RAG
summary: Multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (mRAG) aims to answer image-text queries with external knowledge, but most existing systems still retrieve directly from raw multimodal input over a flat evidence space. This design often struggles with two key challenges: the retrieval target is under-specified because the question intent must be grounded to the correct visual referent, and the search space is weakly structured, forcing semantically distinct evidence to compete in a single global ranking step. We propose MM-R2, a multimodal agentic retrieval framework that reasons before retrieval by explicitly modeling both what to retrieve and where to search. MM-R2 first constructs an intent-grounded retrieval state from the image-question pair, capturing the information need, grounded referent, and retrieval constraints. It then performs retrieval over a structured KnowledgeMap, where the agent selects relevant retrieval units before issuing grounded queries within them. To enable this capability, we build MM-R2-Traj, a large-scale trajectory dataset of multi-step retrieval processes, and adopt a two-stage post-training strategy with supervised fine-tuning and GRPO. Experiments on Infoseek and Encyclopedic VQA datasets show that MM-R2 substantially outperforms strong baselines on answer accuracy while also yielding more interpretable and verifiable retrieval trajectories.

AI.tldr: MM-R2 is a multimodal agentic retrieval framework that reasons before retrieval by modeling what to retrieve and where to search, using intent-grounded retrieval states and a structured KnowledgeMap, achieving superior performance on Infoseek and Encyclopedic VQA datasets.
AI.motivation: Existing mRAG systems struggle with under-specified retrieval targets (question intent not grounded to correct visual referent) and weakly structured search spaces (semantically distinct evidence competing in a single global ranking step).
AI.method: MM-R2 constructs an intent-grounded retrieval state from the image-question pair, then retrieves over a structured KnowledgeMap where the agent selects relevant retrieval units before issuing grounded queries. It uses a two-stage post-training strategy with supervised fine-tuning and GRPO on a large-scale trajectory dataset (MM-R2-Traj).
AI.result: Substantially outperforms strong baselines on answer accuracy on Infoseek and Encyclopedic VQA datasets, with more interpretable and verifiable retrieval trajectories.
AI.conclusion: Reasoning before retrieval with structured search spaces and intent grounding significantly improves mRAG performance and interpretability.

title: Inverse Bayesian Inference for Extracting Lesion Dynamics from Longitudinal Spectral CT
summary:
Longitudinal medical imaging captures temporal evolution of lesions, yet extracting the underlying dynamical parameters governing this evolution remains challenging. We propose an inverse Bayesian framework for inferring lesion dynamics from longitudinal spectral CT. We decompose spectral feature ($x$) evolution into three components: \begin{equation*}
  \frac{dx_i}{dt} = A_i x_i + B \cdot n + C \cdot Δx_{\text{sat}} \end{equation*} where $A_i$ captures intrinsic dynamics (lesion-autonomous evolution), $B$ captures local environment tumour burden (organ tumour burden through satellite count coupling), and $C$ captures environment/satellite state change (i.e., whether surrounding lesions move similarly or not).
  We demonstrate the framework on photon-counting NSCLC CT data from metastases, recovering distinct dynamical regimes: lung lesions exhibit significant satellite count coupling ($B=-0.34$, $p<0.05$) suggesting competitive dynamics, while liver lesions show synergistic satellite behaviour coupling ($C\approx+1.0$, $p<0.05$). Synthetic validation confirms parameter recovery, and cross-coupling analysis validates that our method detects non-zero coupling when present.
  This work establishes inverse dynamical inference as a principled methodology for extracting interpretable parameters from longitudinal imaging, moving beyond static feature extraction toward mechanistic characterisation of lesion behaviour. The code and data are available at: https://github.com/lukasf98/inverse-bayesian-inference

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an inverse Bayesian framework to infer lesion dynamics from longitudinal spectral CT imaging, decomposing feature evolution into intrinsic dynamics, local tumor burden coupling, and environmental state change components. Applied to NSCLC data, it reveals distinct competitive dynamics in lung lesions and synergistic behavior in liver lesions.
AI.motivation: Longitudinal medical imaging captures temporal evolution of lesions, but extracting underlying dynamical parameters governing this evolution remains challenging. Current approaches are limited to static feature extraction rather than mechanistic characterization.
AI.method: An inverse Bayesian framework decomposes spectral feature evolution into three components: intrinsic dynamics (A_i), local environment tumor burden via satellite count coupling (B), and environment/satellite state change (C). The framework is validated on photon-counting NSCLC CT data from metastases.
AI.result: Lung lesions show significant satellite count coupling (B=-0.34, p<0.05) suggesting competitive dynamics, while liver lesions show synergistic satellite behavior coupling (C≈+1.0, p<0.05). Synthetic validation confirms parameter recovery and cross-coupling analysis validates non-zero coupling detection.
AI.conclusion: This work establishes inverse dynamical inference as a principled methodology for extracting interpretable parameters from longitudinal imaging, moving beyond static feature extraction toward mechanistic characterization of lesion behavior.

title: Domain-Prior-Regularized Graph Modeling for Anomaly Detection in Cyber-Physical Systems
comment: 12 pages, ICML 2026 AI for Science Workshop
summary: Anomaly detection on multivariate sensor time series is critical for industrial monitoring of cyber-physical systems (CPS), where even subtle deviations from normal behavior can indicate process disruption. Recent graph-based approaches have made significant progress, but they often struggle in small-scale physical systems with scarce labeled anomalies and limited normal data. In such settings, graph-based models tend to capture spurious correlations and produce unstable sensor topologies. We propose DPR-GM (Domain-Prior-Regularized Graph Modeling), a forecasting-based framework that incorporates system design knowledge into graph construction. DPR-GM leverages a large language model (LLM) to extract directed physical couplings between sensor pairs from system documentation, which are encoded as a binary domain adjacency matrix serving as a structural gate over sensor relations. This gate is then modulated by Pearson correlations estimated from normal training data. The anomaly score is further weighted by sensor-level reliability derived from the coefficient of variation. All graph and weighting components are fixed prior to training and add no learnable parameters. On the SKAB benchmark, DPR-GM outperforms graph-based, statistical, and deep learning baselines across F1, AUROC, and AUPRC, showing that domain-structured graph priors are a practical alternative to fully learned topologies in data-scarce CPS.

AI.tldr: DPR-GM is a forecasting-based anomaly detection framework that uses LLM-extracted domain knowledge (binary adjacency matrix) as a structural gate modulated by Pearson correlations to guide graph construction for multivariate sensor time series, achieving SOTA on SKAB benchmark without learnable graph parameters.
AI.motivation: Existing graph-based anomaly detection methods struggle in small-scale CPS with scarce labeled anomalies and limited normal data, often capturing spurious correlations and producing unstable sensor topologies.
AI.method: DPR-GM uses LLM to extract directed physical couplings from system documentation as a binary domain adjacency matrix (structural gate), modulated by Pearson correlations from normal training data; anomaly scores are weighted by sensor-level reliability via coefficient of variation; all components are fixed pre-training with no learnable parameters.
AI.result: On SKAB benchmark, DPR-GM outperforms graph-based, statistical, and deep learning baselines across F1, AUROC, and AUPRC.
AI.conclusion: Domain-structured graph priors are a practical alternative to fully learned topologies in data-scarce CPS settings.

title: DocHRL: A Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning Framework for Cost-Optimised Document Classification
summary: Real-world document classification pipelines typically apply the same sequence of models to every incoming document, regardless of its complexity or type. This leads to inefficient use of compute and human resources: simple documents are over-processed while difficult ones may not receive enough scrutiny. We introduce DocHRL, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that learns to adaptively and dynamically select the most cost-effective classification policy on a per-document basis. DocHRL formulates document classification as a sequential decision problem with a two-level policy hierarchy: a top-level policy selects among broad options (vision classifiers, LLMs, OCR, and human-in-the-loop review), while option-specific sub-policies choose the concrete model or tool to invoke. The reward signal is the negative total expected cost, which captures inference cost, cost of misclassification, and cost of human labelling. Trained with Proximal Policy Optimisation on the RVL-CDIP benchmark, DocHRL achieves a macro F1 of 0.973 across 16 document classes while reducing average per-document cost to 2.74 normalised units compared to substantially higher costs incurred by fixed standalone classifiers. Our results demonstrate that cost-aware reinforcement learning can simultaneously improve classification performance and operational efficiency in document understanding systems.

AI.tldr: DocHRL is a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that dynamically selects cost-effective document classification policies per document, achieving 0.973 macro F1 at 2.74 normalized cost per document on RVL-CDIP, outperforming fixed standalone classifiers in both accuracy and efficiency.
AI.motivation: Real-world document classification pipelines apply the same sequence of models to all documents regardless of complexity, leading to inefficient compute/resource usage where simple documents are over-processed and difficult ones may lack sufficient scrutiny.
AI.method: DocHRL formulates document classification as a sequential decision problem with a two-level policy hierarchy: a top-level policy selects among broad options (vision classifiers, LLMs, OCR, human review), and option-specific sub-policies choose the concrete model/tool. Trained with Proximal Policy Optimisation, the reward is negative total expected cost (inference + misclassification + human labeling costs).
AI.result: Achieves 0.973 macro F1 across 16 document classes on RVL-CDIP benchmark with average per-document cost of 2.74 normalized units, substantially lower than fixed standalone classifiers.
AI.conclusion: Cost-aware reinforcement learning can simultaneously improve classification performance and operational efficiency in document understanding systems by adaptively selecting policies per document.

title: SHReg: Strictly Rotation-Equivariant Point Cloud Registration via Spherical Harmonics
summary: Point cloud registration critically depends on local features that are both distinctive and robust to arbitrary 3D rotations. Existing learning-based methods typically approximate rotation invariance via fragile local reference frames or extensive data augmentation, providing only empirical invariance and often degrading under unseen rotational transformations. In this paper, we propose SHReg, a strictly rotation-equivariant point cloud registration framework grounded in the representation theory of $SO(3)$. By representing local geometric features as irreducible representations of $SO(3)$, SHReg guarantees exact equivariance under arbitrary rotations without relying on local reference frames. Built upon a spherical-harmonics-based equivariant backbone, SHReg jointly learns rotation-invariant descriptors for robust correspondence matching and rotation-equivariant features that preserve fine-grained orientation information. The preserved equivariant structure enables each correspondence to directly hypothesize a rigid transformation, reducing reliance on large-scale hypothesis sampling in conventional RANSAC-based pipelines and leading to improved robustness under challenging rotational variations. Extensive experiments on 3DMatch, 3DLoMatch, and KITTI demonstrate that SHReg consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in registration accuracy, particularly under large rotational perturbations.

AI.tldr: SHReg proposes a strictly rotation-equivariant point cloud registration framework using spherical harmonics and SO(3) representation theory, achieving exact equivariance and outperforming SOTA methods on 3DMatch, 3DLoMatch, and KITTI.
AI.motivation: Existing learning-based methods for point cloud registration rely on fragile local reference frames or data augmentation for rotation invariance, providing only empirical robustness that degrades under unseen rotations.
AI.method: SHReg uses a spherical-harmonics-based equivariant backbone to represent local geometric features as irreducible representations of SO(3), jointly learning rotation-invariant descriptors for correspondence matching and rotation-equivariant features that preserve orientation, enabling each correspondence to directly hypothesize a rigid transformation without RANSAC.
AI.result: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on 3DMatch, 3DLoMatch, and KITTI benchmarks, especially under large rotational perturbations.
AI.conclusion: Strict rotation equivariance via representation theory is a principled and effective alternative to empirical augmentation-based approaches, improving both robustness and efficiency in point cloud registration.

title: Variance-Preserving Orthogonal Selection (VPOS): Greedy Feature Selection via Orthogonal Deflation in PCA Loading Space
summary: We propose Variance-Preserving Orthogonal Selection (VPOS), a greedy framework for unsupervised feature selection that operates in the weighted PCA loading space. After each selection, VPOS projects out the chosen feature's variance direction via null-space deflation, forcing subsequent selections to cover orthogonal parts of the covariance structure. Each step provably reduces the loading matrix rank by one, and the greedy objective connects to monotone submodular maximization. The single hyperparameter $d$ is selected via a reproducible rule: the value minimising reconstruction MSE in a sensitivity sweep. On eight benchmarks, VPOS achieves the lowest reconstruction MSE on all eight while running 10-140x faster than graph-based methods at scale. Comparing against PCA (no deflation) at matched $d$ confirms deflation as the primary driver, reducing MSE by 10-73%.

AI.tldr: VPOS is a fast, greedy unsupervised feature selection method that uses weighted PCA with orthogonal deflation, achieving the lowest reconstruction MSE on all eight benchmarks while running 10-140x faster than graph-based methods.
AI.motivation: To develop an unsupervised feature selection method that greedily selects orthogonal features via null-space deflation in the PCA loading space, with provable rank reduction and submodular optimization properties.
AI.method: VPOS operates in weighted PCA loading space; after each selection, it projects out the chosen feature's variance direction via null-space deflation; the hyperparameter d is selected via a reproducible rule minimizing reconstruction MSE in a sensitivity sweep.
AI.result: On eight benchmarks, VPOS achieves the lowest reconstruction MSE on all eight, runs 10-140x faster than graph-based methods, and deflation reduces MSE by 10-73% compared to PCA without deflation.
AI.conclusion: VPOS is an efficient and effective unsupervised feature selection method where orthogonal deflation in PCA loading space is the primary driver of performance gains.

title: Extracting Algorithms in Pre-trained LLMs: A Case on Hidden Markov Models
summary: Large language models (LLMs) display a striking ability to predict next observations from Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) via in-context learning (ICL), but the algorithm underlying this capability remains undetermined: prior work has proposed several candidates without consensus, and none has been grounded in the model's internal activations. We close this gap with a three-stage pipeline. First, we empirically compare LLM behavior against a suite of candidate algorithms and narrow the space to three classes -- though no single class explains LLM behavior across all HMM settings and sequence lengths. Second, we derive theoretical connections between the three classes and show how each can be implemented in-context by a Transformer, validating the construction in a small trained Transformer. Third, returning to pre-trained LLMs, we introduce the Principal Activations Probe (PAP), a layer-wise probing and intervention method that isolates algorithmic signals in model activations. PAP reveals low-dimensional linear representations that causally drive model predictions and track empirical ICL performance. PAP further reveals how these representations shift with properties of the underlying HMM regime; distinct computational stages are localized to different layers. Together, our results connect the in-context behavior of pre-trained LLMs to the underlying internal mechanisms and advance our understanding of how LLMs perform ICL on HMMs.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies the algorithm behind LLMs' in-context learning on Hidden Markov Models by narrowing candidate algorithms to three classes, proving theoretical connections between them, and introducing Principal Activations Probe (PAP) to reveal low-dimensional linear representations in model activations that causally drive predictions.
AI.motivation: Prior work has proposed multiple candidate algorithms for how LLMs perform ICL on HMMs, but no consensus exists and none has been grounded in the model's internal activations.
AI.method: Three-stage pipeline: (1) empirical comparison of LLM behavior vs candidate algorithms; (2) theoretical derivation connecting algorithm classes and validation in small trained Transformer; (3) Principal Activations Probe (PAP) for layer-wise probing and intervention.
AI.result: Three algorithm classes explain LLM behavior across different HMM settings and sequence lengths; PAP reveals low-dimensional linear representations that causally drive predictions and track ICL performance; representations shift with HMM regime properties across distinct layers.
AI.conclusion: Connects in-context behavior of pre-trained LLMs to underlying internal mechanisms, advancing understanding of how LLMs perform ICL on HMMs.

title: DispatchRAG: Grounding Emergency Dispatch Decisions in Real-World Protocols from Traffic Accident Video
summary: Assessing the severity of a traffic accident scenario is important to decide which emergency service to dispatch. Missing an ambulance dispatch on a pedestrian accident is a fatal issue that can lead to death. Recently, Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have been a promising tool for accident reasoning, yet many VLMs are not grounded in real-life accident response protocols, making them not usable in accident severity assessment off-the-shelf. We introduced DispatchRAG, an accident assessor and dispatcher framework grounded in real-life Japanese traffic-accident response protocols, designed to enhance VLMs to generate an appropriate emergency response during an emergency scenario. Utilizing a RAG-based retrieval mechanism to retrieve the most relevant accident protocol and an LLM-powered reasoner to suggest the most proper response. To support evaluation, we introduce Accident Dispatch Dataset, a comprehensive dataset of accident assessment and emergency response according to Japanese accident response protocols adapted from the MM-AU dataset. We validate our framework on the Accident Dispatch Dataset, showing strong performance across various accident scenarios compared to the baseline VLM, pointing toward integration in autonomous vehicles that can automatically report both their own and nearby accidents.

AI.tldr: DispatchRAG is a framework that enhances Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for traffic accident severity assessment and emergency response dispatching by grounding them in real-life Japanese accident response protocols using RAG-based retrieval and LLM-powered reasoning, validated on the new Accident Dispatch Dataset.
AI.motivation: Assessing traffic accident severity is critical for appropriate emergency dispatch (e.g., ambulances), but current VLMs lack grounding in real-life accident response protocols, making them unsuitable for off-the-shelf use in this domain.
AI.method: DispatchRAG combines a RAG-based retrieval mechanism to fetch the most relevant accident protocol from Japanese traffic-accident response guidelines, with an LLM-powered reasoner that suggests the appropriate emergency response.
AI.result: The framework demonstrated strong performance across various accident scenarios on the Accident Dispatch Dataset, outperforming baseline VLMs.
AI.conclusion: DispatchRAG shows potential for integration into autonomous vehicles for automatic reporting of both own and nearby accidents, improving emergency response alignment with real-world protocols.

title: ParasGB: A Graph Benchmark Suite for Parasitic Estimation on AMS Circuits
comment: Published at ICCAD2026. Full appendix version
summary: As chip manufacturing processes advance to deep submicron nodes, parasitic interconnect effects increasingly dominate the performance of analog and mixed-signal (AMS) circuits and often lead to costly layout iterations. This makes early-stage estimation of parasitic capacitance and resistance important for parasitic-aware design exploration before full physical implementation. However, progress on GNN-based parasitic modeling has been hindered by the lack of public, high-fidelity RC benchmarks that support reproducible evaluation. To address this gap, we introduce ParasGB, the first open-source benchmark suite for pre-layout parasitic parameter prediction on circuit graphs. ParasGB provides large-scale, heterogeneous RC networks extracted with commercial EDA tools from tape-out-proven designs, together with a unified evaluation protocol covering node-level ground capacitance, edge-level resistance, and edge-level coupling capacitance. Within this framework, we benchmark diverse GNN architectures using a standardized training pipeline and expose challenges such as extreme label imbalance, long-tailed parasitic distributions, and strong structural heterogeneity. By establishing a physically grounded and standardized benchmark for early-stage parasitic prediction, ParasGB provides an open platform for reproducible research on circuit graph learning and parasitic-aware model development. All datasets, preprocessing scripts, and configurations are publicly available in our code repository https://github.com/ShenShan123/ParasGB.git.

AI.tldr: ParasGB is the first open-source benchmark suite for pre-layout parasitic parameter prediction on circuit graphs, providing large-scale RC networks from tape-out-proven designs with a unified evaluation protocol to enable reproducible research on GNN-based parasitic modeling.
AI.motivation: As chip manufacturing advances to deep submicron nodes, parasitic interconnect effects dominate AMS circuit performance and cause costly layout iterations. Early-stage parasitic estimation is crucial, but progress on GNN-based parasitic modeling is hindered by the lack of public, high-fidelity RC benchmarks for reproducible evaluation.
AI.method: ParasGB provides large-scale, heterogeneous RC networks extracted with commercial EDA tools from tape-out-proven designs, with a unified evaluation protocol covering node-level ground capacitance, edge-level resistance, and edge-level coupling capacitance. Diverse GNN architectures are benchmarked using a standardized training pipeline.
AI.result: The benchmark exposes challenges such as extreme label imbalance, long-tailed parasitic distributions, and strong structural heterogeneity in circuit graphs.
AI.conclusion: ParasGB establishes a physically grounded and standardized benchmark for early-stage parasitic prediction, providing an open platform for reproducible research on circuit graph learning and parasitic-aware model development. All datasets, scripts, and configurations are publicly available.

title: PTStore (Prefix Tensor Store): Distributed Prefix Caching and Replication for High Throughput Inference Serving
summary: Inspired by the design of client caching in Content Delivery Networks (CDNs), PTStore distributes and replicates popular tensors that form reusable KV cache prefixes, which are the main technique used by state of art approaches to accelerate inferences. This reduces the latency of accessing the KV cache and alleviates load imbalance caused by a disproportionately large number of requests on servers containing popular tensors. Furthermore, thanks to decentralization, PTStore allows the expansion of the size of the KV cache for LLM inference by orders of magnitude. As a result, PTStore can execute inferences on long passage Q\&A datasets 5-6 times more efficiently than current baselines, which do not aggregate memory across different nodes and GPUs and therefore require regenerating the KV cache.

AI.tldr: PTStore is a decentralized system inspired by CDN caching that distributes and replicates popular KV cache prefix tensors across nodes, enabling 5-6x more efficient LLM inference on long passage Q&A by reducing latency, alleviating load imbalance, and scaling cache size orders of magnitude beyond current baselines that require cache regeneration.
AI.motivation: Current LLM inference systems face high latency from regenerating KV cache for long sequences, and load imbalance due to concentrated requests on servers hosting popular tensors. Existing approaches lack cross-node memory aggregation.
AI.method: PTStore adopts CDN-inspired client caching by distributing and replicating reusable KV cache prefix tensors across decentralized nodes, enabling memory aggregation across different GPUs and nodes.
AI.result: PTStore executes inferences on long passage Q&A datasets 5-6 times more efficiently than baselines that lack cross-node memory aggregation and require KV cache regeneration.
AI.conclusion: Decentralized KV cache distribution and replication can significantly improve LLM inference efficiency for long-context tasks by reducing latency, balancing load, and scaling cache capacity.

title: Towards Dual-Brain Minimal Sufficient Representation for Vision-Language Navigation
summary: Vision-and-Language Navigation in continuous environments (VLN-CE) requires an agent to ground language in egocentric observations and plan in unseen scenes. Although recent multimodal large models and world-model-based methods have improved navigation, they often preserve excessive task-irrelevant detail, weakening generalization and increasing computational burden. We propose BrainNav, a navigation framework grounded in the Principle of Minimal Sufficiency. BrainNav consists of three components: a Logical Anchor Model that implements instruction-aware selective perception to suppress environmental noise, a Minimalist Constraint Alignment module that serves as a compact cross-modal bottleneck, efficiently synchronizing discrete linguistic intent with continuous latent dynamics while filtering out redundant information, and a Compression World Model that predicts action-conditioned states within a condensed, low-rank latent space. These modules align semantic intent with spatial perception, enhancing the agent's robustness and efficiency in complex tasks. Experiments show that BrainNav improves over prior SOTA by 2.0 % / 1.0 in SR/SPL on R2R-CE val-unseen and 0.94 % / 0.78 on RxR-CE val-unseen. These results indicate that minimally sufficient world representations provide an effective foundation for robust VLN.

AI.tldr: BrainNav proposes a navigation framework based on the Principle of Minimal Sufficiency, using three components (Logical Anchor Model, Minimalist Constraint Alignment, Compression World Model) to filter redundant information and achieve efficient VLN-CE, improving over prior SOTA by 2.0%/1.0 on R2R-CE and 0.94%/0.78 on RxR-CE.
AI.motivation: Existing VLN-CE methods using multimodal large models and world-model-based approaches preserve excessive task-irrelevant detail, which weakens generalization and increases computational burden.
AI.method: BrainNav implements the Principle of Minimal Sufficiency via three modules: (1) Logical Anchor Model for instruction-aware selective perception to suppress environmental noise; (2) Minimalist Constraint Alignment as a compact cross-modal bottleneck synchronizing discrete linguistic intent with continuous latent dynamics; (3) Compression World Model for predicting action-conditioned states in a condensed low-rank latent space.
AI.result: BrainNav achieves 2.0%/1.0 improvement in SR/SPL on R2R-CE val-unseen and 0.94%/0.78 on RxR-CE val-unseen over prior SOTA.
AI.conclusion: Minimally sufficient world representations provide an effective foundation for robust vision-and-language navigation in continuous environments.

title: From Score Learning to Discretized Sampling: An End-to-End Generalization Analysis of Diffusion Models
summary: Despite the empirical success of score-based diffusion models, a complete theoretical understanding of how finite-sample learning, network parameterization, and numerical discretization jointly dictate generative quality remains underdeveloped. Existing sampling analyses often evaluate the generative performance conditional on an oracle score or a pre-specified error threshold. In this work, we establish a unified convergence and generalization framework for score-based diffusion models parameterized by practical ResNet-type architectures. We analyze the generalization and convergence properties from the practical finite-sample, discrete-time learning problem of the score function to the ideal continuous-time, population-level objective. Based on the generalization result of the learning problem of score function, we analyze the sampling process induced by the learned score function and provide an end-to-end total variation distance estimate for the generated terminal distribution. This estimate explicitly decomposes the overall generative error into four interpretable components: the truncation error of the forward process, the reverse-time discretization error, the generalization error incorporating both finite data and forward-time discretization, and the training optimization gap. Our results quantitatively characterize how the training sample size, temporal discretization grids, and optimization accuracy jointly control the final fidelity of samples generated by diffusion models.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a unified theoretical framework for score-based diffusion models with ResNet-type architectures, providing an end-to-end total variation distance bound that decomposes generative error into truncation, discretization, generalization, and optimization components, and characterizing how sample size, discretization grids, and optimization accuracy jointly affect sample quality.
AI.motivation: Existing theoretical analyses of diffusion models either assume oracle score functions or pre-specified error thresholds, lacking a complete understanding of how finite-sample learning, network parameterization, and numerical discretization jointly determine generative quality.
AI.method: The authors develop a unified convergence and generalization framework for score-based diffusion models using practical ResNet-type architectures, analyzing generalization from finite-sample discrete-time learning to the ideal continuous-time population-level objective, and then providing end-to-end total variation distance estimation via error decomposition into four components.
AI.result: An end-to-end total variation distance estimate for the generated terminal distribution that explicitly decomposes overall generative error into truncation error of the forward process, reverse-time discretization error, generalization error (incorporating finite data and forward-time discretization), and training optimization gap.
AI.conclusion: The training sample size, temporal discretization grids, and optimization accuracy jointly control the final fidelity of samples generated by diffusion models, providing quantitative guidance for practical implementations.

title: STAIF: A Stage-wise Optimization for Complex Instruction Following
summary: Following complex instructions with multiple explicit constraints remains a fundamental challenge for large language models (LLMs). Existing alignment methods, such as DPO, optimize holistic reward signals that often underemphasize strict satisfaction of individual constraints, particularly under out-of-distribution or multi-constraint settings. In this paper, we propose STAIF, a stage-wise optimization framework that decouples the alignment of subjective (soft) constraints from the optimization of objectively verifiable (hard) constraints. Stage 1 applies preference optimization with multiple negative samples to sharpen sensitivity to soft constraints, while Stage 2 applies Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) to enforce strict compliance with hard constraints. To support this method, we construct STAINSTRUCT, a high-quality bilingual (English, Chinese) dataset of approximately 31,000 complex multi-constraint instructions. Extensive analyses validate the design of STAIF and show state-of-the-art performance on representative benchmarks against strong baselines, as well as genuine generalization.

AI.tldr: STAIF is a stage-wise framework that decouples alignment of soft (subjective) and hard (verifiable) constraints for LLMs, outperforming baselines on multi-constraint instruction following using a new bilingual dataset STAINSTRUCT.
AI.motivation: LLMs struggle with complex multi-constraint instructions; existing alignment methods like DPO underemphasize individual constraint satisfaction, especially under out-of-distribution or multi-constraint settings.
AI.method: A two-stage optimization framework: Stage 1 uses preference optimization with multiple negative samples to improve soft constraint sensitivity; Stage 2 applies Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) to enforce hard constraint compliance. A bilingual dataset STAINSTRUCT (~31K complex multi-constraint instructions) is constructed to support training.
AI.result: State-of-the-art performance on representative benchmarks against strong baselines, with demonstrated generalization capabilities.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling soft and hard constraint alignment via stage-wise optimization effectively improves multi-constraint instruction following in LLMs.

title: Fashion-3DLR: A Controllable 3D Garment Generation Using Pairwise Fashion Elements for Intelligent Design
summary: AI-generated content (AIGC) has made significant progress, with 2D generative models becoming ready-to-use tools for the digital fashion industry. However, 3D garment generation remains in its nascent stage, where in the realm of fashion, the semantic information of diverse design elements exhibits intricate coupling relationships in 3D representations, posing substantial challenges for generating diverse 3D garments. In this work, to handle the above problem, We introduce Fashion-3DLR, a novel 3D garment generation framework that utilizes diverse design elements to create high-quality, versatile 3D garment assets. Specifically, to bridge the semantic gaps between different fashion elements, we propose a Garment Feature Fusion Diffusion Transformer (GFF-DiT) module to integrate 2D fashion design elements, e.g., sketch and texture, into latent space. Within the latent space, we then employ a rectified flow transformer to generate geometry latents, which can be decoded into various 3D garment representations, including 3D Gaussians and meshes. Furthermore, we integrate Fashion-3DLR into downstream tasks, achieving the 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)-driven cloth physical simulation and mesh-based virtual try-on. Experimental results indicate that Fashion-3DLR surpass the previous state-of-the-art methods, which verify that the proposed work can generate well-structured, non-watertight garments capable of physical simulation and virtual try-on, underscoring its potential as a versatile 3D garment design tool.

AI.tldr: Fashion-3DLR is a novel 3D garment generation framework that uses a Garment Feature Fusion Diffusion Transformer (GFF-DiT) to integrate 2D design elements (sketch, texture) into a latent space, then employs a rectified flow transformer to generate geometry latents decoded into 3D Gaussians and meshes, enabling physical simulation and virtual try-on, outperforming prior SOTA methods.
AI.motivation: 3D garment generation is challenging because semantic information of diverse design elements exhibits intricate coupling relationships in 3D representations; existing methods cannot handle the semantic gaps between different fashion elements effectively.
AI.method: Proposes Fashion-3DLR framework with a Garment Feature Fusion Diffusion Transformer (GFF-DiT) to fuse 2D fashion elements (sketch, texture) into latent space, then uses a rectified flow transformer to generate geometry latents decoded into 3D Gaussians and meshes.
AI.result: Surpasses previous state-of-the-art methods; generates well-structured, non-watertight garments capable of physical simulation and virtual try-on.
AI.conclusion: Fashion-3DLR is a versatile 3D garment design tool that bridges semantic gaps between design elements and supports downstream tasks like 3DGS-driven cloth simulation and mesh-based virtual try-on.

title: Context-Aware Concept Distillation for Trustworthy Flood Prediction
comment: to be published in IJCAI 2026 proceedings
summary: Effective flood risk management relies on accurate forecasting, yet the "black box" nature of stateof-the-art Deep Learning models creates a barrier to trust and accountability in high-stakes public safety decisions. While existing Explainable AI (XAI) methods offer local attributions, they fail to provide the verifiable, operationally meaningful causal narratives required by disaster response authorities. To address this societal challenge, we propose Context-Aware Concept Distillation (CACD), a framework developed in collaboration with domain experts to distill opaque LSTMs into interpretable, hydrology-aware surrogate models. We introduce an unsupervised pipeline to discover a "Hydrological Language" and a Residual Hypernetwork that dynamically modulates these concepts based on static basin characteristics. Evaluated on 5,203 basins globally, our model achieves high fidelity (Median NSE 0.70), significantly outperforming black-box baselines (e.g., Multi Layer Perceptrons) on unseen future data. By demonstrating that human-interpretable concepts are sufficient to reconstruct flood dynamics, this work balances AI accuracy with the transparency required for responsible environmental decision-making.

AI.tldr: CACD framework distills opaque LSTMs into interpretable, hydrology-aware surrogate models using a discovered "Hydrological Language" and Residual Hypernetwork, achieving high fidelity (Median NSE 0.70) on 5,203 global basins while providing verifiable, causal narratives for flood risk management.
AI.motivation: The "black box" nature of Deep Learning models creates a barrier to trust and accountability in high-stakes public safety decisions like flood risk management, as existing XAI methods fail to provide verifiable, operationally meaningful causal narratives required by disaster response authorities.
AI.method: CACD uses an unsupervised pipeline to discover a "Hydrological Language" (interpretable concepts) and a Residual Hypernetwork that dynamically modulates these concepts based on static basin characteristics, distilling opaque LSTMs into interpretable, hydrology-aware surrogate models.
AI.result: Evaluated on 5,203 basins globally, the model achieves high fidelity (Median NSE 0.70), significantly outperforming black-box baselines (e.g., MLPs) on unseen future data.
AI.conclusion: Human-interpretable concepts are sufficient to reconstruct flood dynamics, balancing AI accuracy with the transparency required for responsible environmental decision-making.

title: ARdena: Scenario-driven control of real-time LLM agents
summary: Large language models (LLMs) have enabled increasingly capable conversational agents, but reliably controlling their behavior in real-time interactive environments remains a significant challenge. Existing approaches often rely on model fine-tuning or alignment procedures that are difficult to adapt to changing interaction requirements. This paper introduces layered scenario-driven LLM control, a framework that enables runtime behavior control through structured prompting. By combining persistent context with scenario-specific constraints, the approach allows agent behavior to be modified during interaction without changing the underlying model. The framework is implemented in ARDena, a real-time multimodal embodied agent that integrates speech interaction, visual perception, tool use, and avatar-based response generation. The proposed approach is evaluated with respect to control effectiveness, response latency, and operational stability. The results demonstrate that scenario definitions alone can produce substantially different interaction behaviors while maintaining stable real-time operation, highlighting the effectiveness of scenario-driven prompting for controlling LLM agents.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces layered scenario-driven LLM control, a framework for runtime behavior control through structured prompting, implemented in ARDena—a real-time multimodal embodied agent. Results show scenario definitions alone can produce substantially different interaction behaviors while maintaining stable real-time operation.
AI.motivation: Reliably controlling LLM-based conversational agents in real-time interactive environments remains challenging; existing methods like fine-tuning or alignment are difficult to adapt to changing interaction requirements.
AI.method: Layered scenario-driven LLM control combines persistent context with scenario-specific constraints via structured prompting, enabling runtime behavior modification without model changes. Implemented in ARDena, a real-time multimodal embodied agent integrating speech, vision, tool use, and avatar responses.
AI.result: Scenario definitions alone produce substantially different interaction behaviors while maintaining stable real-time operation with controlled response latency and operational stability.
AI.conclusion: Scenario-driven prompting is effective for controlling LLM agents at runtime, offering a flexible alternative to fine-tuning or alignment-based approaches for adaptive behavior control.

title: OmniScope: Modality-Decoupled Token Compression for Omnimodal Large Language Models
summary: Existing token compression methods for omnimodal large language models typically rely on one modality to determine what to retain in the other. We show that this assumption often breaks down: for the same query, audio and video relevance often peaks at different moments. This cross-modal salience mismatch makes unidirectional guidance prone to discarding answer-critical cues under aggressive compression. We propose OmniScope, a training-free token compression framework that uses the query as a shared semantic anchor while estimating relevance separately for audio and video. OmniScope allocates modality-specific token budgets, prunes visual tokens with an anchor-delta strategy that preserves both global context and temporal changes, and merges audio tokens within each second to reduce redundancy while maintaining temporal continuity. Across four audio-video benchmarks and two Qwen2.5-Omni model scales, OmniScope achieves the best average accuracy across all compression settings. At 25% overall token retention, it delivers up to 3.53x prefill speedup and more than 15% GPU memory reduction, with only a 0.35-point drop in average accuracy. These results suggest a simple design principle for OmniLLM inference: share the query across modalities, but not the salience estimates. The code is available at https://github.com/MAC-AutoML/OmniScope.

AI.tldr: OmniScope is a training-free token compression framework for omniLLMs that estimates relevance separately for audio and video using the query as a shared anchor. At 25% token retention, it achieves up to 3.53x prefill speedup and >15% GPU memory reduction with only 0.35 avg accuracy drop.
AI.motivation: Existing token compression methods for omniLLMs rely on one modality to guide retention in another, but cross-modal salience mismatch causes answer-critical cues to be discarded under aggressive compression.
AI.method: Query-based shared semantic anchor with modality-specific relevance estimation; anchor-delta strategy for visual pruning (global context + temporal changes); per-second audio token merging.
AI.result: Best average accuracy across 4 benchmarks and 2 Qwen2.5-Omni scales; at 25% retention: 3.53x prefill speedup, >15% GPU memory reduction, 0.35 avg accuracy drop.
AI.conclusion: Design principle: share the query across modalities, but not the salience estimates.

title: StageGuard: Physiologically Constrained Sleep Staging
comment: 12 pages. Accepted at KDD 2026 (32nd ACM SIGKDD Conference), AI for Sciences track
summary: Automated sleep staging is increasingly used in large-scale studies to derive sleep-architecture endpoints: total sleep time, REM latency, sleep efficiency, and bout-duration statistics. Deep learning models achieve epoch-level accuracy approaching inter-rater agreement, yet often produce hypnograms that violate physiological invariants, such as rare transitions (e.g., direct Wake -> REM) or excessively fragmented sequences. Such violations can bias downstream sleep metrics, regardless of overall accuracy. We propose StageGuard, a plug-and-play, backbone-agnostic structured-inference framework that wraps any neural sleep-staging backbone with physiology-informed priors. StageGuard combines (1) a differentiable soft transition penalty that discourages physiologically rare transitions during training, and (2) a semi-Markov constrained decoder with a duration-augmented state space that jointly enforces transition penalties and minimum bout durations at inference. Unlike hard-prohibition methods, it admits rare transitions when emission evidence is overwhelming, leaving informative pathological events recoverable rather than blocked. StageGuard constrains staging outputs to satisfy known physiological priors rather than modeling sleep generatively. We quantify the validity gap using transition-violation rate (TVR) and fragmentation index (FI) and demonstrate that, across six backbones and four datasets, StageGuard reduces TVR to physiologically plausible levels and lowers FI by 56-62%, while maintaining or slightly improving classification accuracy. Crucially, improved constraint satisfaction translates into 59-79% lower error on derived sleep-architecture statistics not directly optimized by the method, and recovers the direction and effect size of expert-defined subgroup differences (OSA severity, age) more faithfully than the unconstrained baseline.

AI.tldr: StageGuard is a plug-and-play structured-inference framework that wraps neural sleep-staging models with physiology-informed priors to enforce valid hypnogram transitions and minimum bout durations, reducing transition-violation rates and fragmentation by 56-62% while improving downstream sleep-architecture metric accuracy by 59-79% across six backbones and four datasets.
AI.motivation: Deep learning sleep staging models achieve high epoch-level accuracy but produce hypnograms violating physiological invariants (e.g., rare transitions, excessive fragmentation), which bias downstream sleep-architecture metrics regardless of overall accuracy. Existing methods lack physiological constraints to address this validity gap.
AI.method: StageGuard combines (1) a differentiable soft transition penalty for training that discourages rare transitions, and (2) a semi-Markov constrained decoder with duration-augmented state space enforcing transition penalties and minimum bout durations at inference. It is backbone-agnostic and uses soft rather than hard constraints to preserve informative pathological events.
AI.result: Across six backbones and four datasets, StageGuard reduces transition-violation rate (TVR) to physiologically plausible levels, lowers fragmentation index (FI) by 56-62%, maintains or slightly improves classification accuracy, reduces error on derived sleep-architecture statistics by 59-79%, and recovers expert-defined subgroup differences (OSA severity, age) more faithfully than unconstrained baselines.
AI.conclusion: Enforcing physiological priors on neural sleep staging outputs through structured inference effectively closes the validity gap between epoch-level accuracy and clinically meaningful sleep-architecture endpoints, producing more reliable biomarkers for large-scale studies.

title: KG2Code: Bridging Knowledge Graphs and Large Language Models via Executable Code for Question Answering
summary: Recent research has explored the integration of knowledge graphs (KGs) with large language models (LLMs) to enhance their performance on downstream knowledge-intensive tasks, particularly knowledge graph question answering (KGQA). Existing approaches primarily combine LLMs with KGs through retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-based, agent-based, and SPARQL-based methods. Although these methods have achieved notable success, they still suffer from several limitations, including structural information loss, unfaithful reasoning, and limited flexibility and generalization. To address these challenges, this paper proposes KG2Code, a novel approach that transforms knowledge graphs into a code-based representation, preserving structural semantics while naturally aligning with the code-aware pretraining of modern LLMs. Based on KG2Code, KG2Code-QA is further introduced as a KGQA framework that formulates KGQA as a code generation task. This formulation enables the generation of verifiable reasoning traces and executable code, thereby substantially mitigating the impact of hallucinations. In addition, an automated pipeline is developed to construct a large-scale, high-quality code corpus for effectively training open-source LLMs on KG2Code-QA. After training, LLMs are able to perform KGQA in zero-shot scenarios. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly outperforms existing KG-enhanced LLM methods for KGQA, while exhibiting strong generalization to unseen KGs. The code and data are available at Github.

AI.tldr: KG2Code transforms knowledge graphs into code-based representations to formulate KGQA as a code generation task, outperforming existing KG-enhanced LLM methods with strong generalization to unseen KGs.
AI.motivation: Existing KG-enhanced LLM methods (RAG-based, agent-based, SPARQL-based) suffer from structural information loss, unfaithful reasoning, and limited flexibility/generalization when addressing knowledge graph question answering.
AI.method: Proposes KG2Code to convert KGs into code representations aligned with code-aware pretraining of LLMs, and KG2Code-QA as a KGQA framework that formulates question answering as a code generation task with verifiable reasoning traces and executable code. An automated pipeline constructs a large-scale code corpus for training open-source LLMs.
AI.result: The proposed approach significantly outperforms existing KG-enhanced LLM methods for KGQA and exhibits strong generalization to unseen knowledge graphs.
AI.conclusion: Transforming KGs into code representations effectively addresses structural information loss and hallucination issues in KGQA, enabling zero-shot performance on unseen KGs after training on a constructed code corpus.

title: Out-of-Length Scene Text Recognition: A Two-Axis Diagnosis and a Training-Free Fix
comment: 39 pages, 10 tables, includes supplementary material (folded in as Appendix S1-S4). Code: https://github.com/zobeirraisi/chunk-decode-stitch
summary: Scene Text Recognition (STR) models are trained almost exclusively on word crops of at most 25 characters, yet real deployments (signage, product labels, dense captions) require reading much longer text. This paper diagnoses that failure and then closes it. The diagnosis separates out-of-length failure into two simultaneously extrapolating axes (the encoder's width axis and the decoder's time axis) and shows that encoder width, not decoder length, is the dominant failure mode. Representation-side fixes bring only partial relief: training-free rotary rescalings recover at most 2-4 points of character error rate (CER), and a weighted fine-tuning recipe recovers 6-8 points while improving standard-benchmark accuracy, yet word accuracy on the Long Text Benchmark (LTB) stays near zero, because the residual gap lies in the decoding mechanism rather than the representation. We then close that gap at inference time, on an unmodified word-level checkpoint: the long image is sliced into overlapping crops at the model's training width, each decoded independently and in-distribution, and the reads stitched by geometry-anchored edit-distance alignment. This procedure reaches 42.79-43.05% bucket-average word accuracy on LTB across two base checkpoints, matching the published state of the art (41.57%) and beating it by 11-12 points on the hardest bucket, at wall-clock parity with plain decoding; applied unchanged to the public PARSeq checkpoint it reaches 47.11%. Once chunking is applied fine-tuning no longer helps: the decoding-side fix alone matches purpose-built architectures. We release the diagnosis harness and implementation.

AI.tldr: STR models fail on long text due to encoder width limitations, not decoder length. The paper closes this gap by slicing long images into overlapping crops at training width, decoding independently, and stitching via geometry-anchored edit-distance alignment, achieving 42.79-43.05% accuracy on LTB, matching/beating prior SOTA.
AI.motivation: STR models trained on short word crops (≤25 chars) fail on longer real-world text (signage, labels, dense captions). The paper aims to diagnose and close this out-of-length generalization failure.
AI.method: (1) Diagnosis: separates failure into encoder width extrapolation vs. decoder time axis extrapolation, identifying encoder width as the dominant failure mode. (2) Fixes: training-free rotary rescaling (+2-4 CER), weighted fine-tuning (+6-8 CER). (3) Main solution: inference-time chunking—slice long image into overlapping crops at training width, decode each independently, then stitch reads via geometry-anchored edit-distance alignment.
AI.result: 42.79-43.05% bucket-average word accuracy on LTB across two checkpoints, matching SOTA (41.57%) and beating by 11-12 pts on hardest bucket. Applied to PARSeq: 47.11%. Fine-tuning no longer helps after chunking is applied.
AI.conclusion: The decoding-side fix (chunking+stitching) alone matches purpose-built architectures. The residual gap is in decoding mechanism, not representation. Fine-tuning offers no additional benefit once chunking is applied.

title: FILLER: Feature Imputation via Latent Location Exploration and Retrieval
summary: In real-world machine learning applications, incomplete observations create a fundamental challenge. Researchers have come up with several ideas to address this crucial problem. However, current models still face challenges in balancing scalability and structural consistency. This study proposes a feature imputation method, called FILLER, that deliberately searches the two-dimensional latent space produced by a generative model and fills the missing values with appropriate entries. The generative model is trained on fully observed data to generate samples from the latent space, and FILLER uses this trained model to impute the values missing in the corrupted test samples. In this study, G-NeuroDAVIS serves the purpose of the generative model. This work also presents a mathematical proof on the convergence of the iterative search. Finally, FILLER has been evaluated on several image datasets under random and structured missingness patterns with varying levels of imputation complexities. In order to justify the efficacy of FILLER, it has been compared against existing state-of-the-art solution strategies in terms of RMSE, PSNR, and SSIM. In addition, Wilcoxon signed-rank test has been carried out to validate statistical significance. Moreover, downstream analyses (classification and clustering) have also established the quality of imputation in terms of standard metrics.

AI.tldr: FILLER is a feature imputation method that searches the 2D latent space of a generative model (G-NeuroDAVIS) trained on complete data to fill missing values in corrupted test samples, with mathematical proof of convergence, evaluated on image datasets against state-of-the-art methods using RMSE, PSNR, SSIM, statistical tests, and downstream tasks.
AI.motivation: Incomplete observations challenge real-world ML applications, and existing models struggle to balance scalability with structural consistency during imputation.
AI.method: FILLER performs iterative search over the 2D latent space of a pre-trained generative model (G-NeuroDAVIS) to impute missing values in corrupted test samples; the generative model is trained on fully observed data.
AI.result: Evaluated on image datasets under random and structured missingness patterns; outperformed state-of-the-art methods in RMSE, PSNR, and SSIM; validated with Wilcoxon signed-rank test; downstream classification and clustering confirmed imputation quality.
