AI.tldr: ReflexTrack is a training-free, feedback-driven agent for referring video object segmentation that improves reliability through spatial and temporal prediction-level feedback loops, achieving strong results on Ref-VPS and ReasonVOS benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing agentic RVOS pipelines rely on one-shot spatial grounding followed by mask propagation, leaving initial prompts and temporal predictions largely unverified, leading to unreliable segmentation.
AI.method: ReflexTrack introduces two feedback loops: (1) Mask-guided Spatial Refinement iteratively updates bounding boxes and positive/negative points for reliable initialization; (2) Video-level Mask Reflection assesses the mask sequence, localizes unreliable intervals, selects complementary repair keyframes, and generates candidate predictions via mask-guided re-propagation, accepting only verified improvements.
AI.result: Achieves 69.7 Q score on Ref-VPS and 67.2 J&F score on ReasonVOS.
AI.conclusion: Prediction-level feedback substantially improves the reliability of training-free RVOS.

title: Forecasting the Emergence and Evolution of Crash Hotspots: A Unified Deep Learning Framework for Proactive Traffic Safety
summary: Road crashes remain among the gravest threats to public safety, and preventing them is a defining task of transportation systems worldwide. Much of that harm concentrates at hotspots, yet a hotspot is less a place than an episode; it emerges quietly at an intersection or along an arterial, intensifies for weeks, then subsides, only to reappear elsewhere. Enforcement guided by maps of past crashes inevitably trails this cycle, patrolling yesterday's hotspots while tomorrow's form unwatched. Breaking that lag requires three capabilities at once: detecting hotspots as they are born, forecasting where they will sit next week, and following each one through its life. We introduce HERALD (Hotspot Emergence, Risk Anticipation, and Life-cycle Dynamics), a unified deep learning framework that provides all three from a single statewide model. HERALD distills each county's recent crash history into weekly risk maps and forecasts the next with a CNN--Transformer, whose mixture-of-experts lets one model serve dense urban cores and sparse rural corridors alike. Each forecast is anchored in the county's long-run crash geography, sharpened by the self-exciting effect of recent crashes, and paired with explicit warnings of where new hotspots are about to appear. Followed over time, every hotspot acquires a legible life story, from birth through growth and stability to decline and death. Across six heterogeneous Wisconsin counties, HERALD forecasts more accurately than five identically trained baselines, locates hotspots most precisely, and flags emerging risks before they take hold. A single adjustable setting trades accuracy for extra sensitivity where deployment demands it. The result shifts hotspot management from mapping the past to anticipating the future.

AI.tldr: HERALD is a unified deep learning framework that detects, forecasts, and tracks the full life cycle of road crash hotspots using a CNN-Transformer with mixture-of-experts, outperforming baselines across six Wisconsin counties.
AI.motivation: Traditional crash hotspot management relies on reactive mapping of past crashes, which fails to keep pace with the dynamic, episodic nature of hotspots that emerge, intensify, and subside over time. A proactive approach requires simultaneously detecting nascent hotspots, forecasting their future locations, and tracking their evolution.
AI.method: HERALD uses a CNN-Transformer architecture with a mixture-of-experts design, trained on statewide crash data. It processes weekly crash history into risk maps, anchors forecasts in long-run crash geography, incorporates self-exciting effects of recent crashes, and provides explicit hotspot emergence warnings with life-cycle tracking.
AI.result: Across six heterogeneous Wisconsin counties, HERALD outperforms five identically trained baselines in forecasting accuracy, hotspot localization precision, and early risk detection. A single adjustable parameter enables trade-off between accuracy and sensitivity for deployment needs.
AI.conclusion: HERALD shifts hotspot management from reactive mapping of past crashes to proactive anticipation of future risks by providing unified detection, forecasting, and life-cycle tracking of crash hotspots.

title: From RLVR to RLSVR: Task Transformation Induces Self-Verifiable Rewards for Open-Ended LLM Self-Improvement
summary: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has driven recent progress in reasoning-oriented large language models (LLMs) by enabling large-scale optimization. However, its applicability remains largely limited to domains such as mathematics and coding, where correctness can be deterministically verified. Open-ended tasks instead often rely on human preferences, reward models, or LLM-based judges, introducing evaluation bias, judge capability bottlenecks, and additional inference costs.Drawing on the principle of self-supervised learning, which constructs pretext tasks to derive supervision from the data itself, we propose Reinforcement Learning with Self-Verifiable Rewards (RLSVR), a task-transformation-based training paradigm for extending RLVR to open-ended tasks. RLSVR transforms open-ended tasks into verifiable proxy environments whose internal rules and interaction outcomes automatically generate reward signals. We instantiate RLSVR with SpyRL, a multi-agent self-play environment inspired by Who Is the Spy?. Agents receive asymmetric information, complete the same target task, and vote to identify a designated spy. Because the spy identity is predetermined, voting outcomes provide fully verifiable rewards, while successful identification remains closely related to output quality. Experiments on text summarization, creative writing, and mathematical reasoning show that SpyRL outperforms existing self-improvement methods on non-verifiable tasks and yields consistent gains on verifiable reasoning tasks. These results demonstrate that task transformation can extend scalable RLVR-based self-improvement beyond inherently verifiable domains. Models and code have been released at https://github.com/wangqinsi1/SpyRL.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes Reinforcement Learning with Self-Verifiable Rewards (RLSVR), a task-transformation paradigm that extends RLVR to open-ended tasks. It introduces SpyRL, a multi-agent self-play environment inspired by "Who Is the Spy?" where voting outcomes on a predetermined spy provide verifiable rewards. Experiments on summarization, creative writing, and math reasoning show SpyRL outperforms existing self-improvement methods on non-verifiable tasks while maintaining gains on verifiable reasoning tasks.
AI.motivation: RLVR has driven progress in reasoning LLMs but is limited to verifiable domains (math, coding). Open-ended tasks rely on human preferences, reward models, or LLM judges, which introduce bias, capability bottlenecks, and inference costs. The paper aims to extend RLVR benefits to open-ended tasks without these drawbacks.
AI.method: Proposes RLSVR, a task-transformation paradigm that converts open-ended tasks into verifiable proxy environments with automatic reward signals. Instantiates as SpyRL, a multi-agent self-play game where agents receive asymmetric information, complete the same target task, and vote to identify a designated spy. Since spy identity is predetermined, voting outcomes provide fully verifiable rewards tied to output quality.
AI.result: Experiments on text summarization, creative writing, and mathematical reasoning show SpyRL outperforms existing self-improvement methods on non-verifiable tasks and yields consistent gains on verifiable reasoning tasks.
AI.conclusion: Task transformation can effectively extend scalable RLVR-based self-improvement beyond inherently verifiable domains to open-ended tasks, offering a new training paradigm that avoids traditional evaluation bottlenecks.

title: LU-500: A Logo Benchmark for Concept Unlearning
summary: Concept unlearning is increasingly used to limit the reproduction of protected or unsafe visual concepts in text-to-image models. Existing evaluations, however, mostly study targets that dominate the whole image, such as styles, broad object categories, or portrait-like identities, leaving company logos comparatively underexamined. Logos create a different failure mode: a small localized mark can carry the entire protected concept, must be visually precise to remain recognizable, and can be triggered implicitly by products, storefronts, packaging, or advertisements even when the word ``logo'' is absent. We introduce LU-500, a logo-unlearning benchmark built from Fortune Global 500 companies to study this localized and semantically entangled setting. LU-500 contains nearly 10,000 curated text-query and logo-image pairs, with an explicit track (LUex-500) and an implicit contextual track (LUim-500). To avoid reducing the task to a binary detector score, we define a multi-grained protocol that evaluates both local logo removal and global image preservation in pixel and latent spaces. Experiments on representative inference-time methods, including NP, SLD, and SEGA, and compatible fine-tuning-based methods such as ESD and Forget-Me-Not, show that the evaluated methods struggle to remove logo evidence without changing non-target content. We further analyze ProLU, a prompt-space multi-agent baseline: it improves local erasure by removing logo-inducing semantics, but also illustrates why prompt filtering is not a substitute for weight-level disentanglement. Correlation analyses over logo area, location, and structural complexity suggest that future logo unlearning may need spatially aware controls, such as SSIM-guided constraints, rather than purely global concept suppression.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces LU-500, a logo-unlearning benchmark from Fortune Global 500 companies, revealing that existing concept unlearning methods fail to precisely remove localized logo content without distorting the rest of the image, and that spatial awareness (e.g., SSIM-guided constraints) is needed over global suppression.
AI.motivation: Existing concept unlearning evaluations focus on dominant image targets (styles, objects, portraits), but logos represent a distinct failure mode: they are small, localized, visually precise, and can be triggered implicitly via context (products, packaging, etc.). This underexamined setting demands dedicated study.
AI.method: The authors construct LU-500 from Fortune Global 500 companies with ~10,000 text-query/logo-image pairs, divided into explicit (LUex-500) and implicit contextual (LUim-500) tracks. They define a multi-grained evaluation protocol measuring both local logo removal and global image preservation at pixel and latent levels. They test inference-time methods (NP, SLD, SEGA) and fine-tuning methods (ESD, Forget-Me-Not), plus a prompt-space multi-agent baseline (ProLU).
AI.result: Existing methods struggle to remove logo evidence without altering non-target content. ProLU improves local erasure via prompt filtering but reveals that prompt-level intervention is insufficient compared to weight-level disentanglement. Correlation analyses over logo area, location, and structural complexity indicate spatial awareness is needed.
AI.conclusion: Future logo unlearning likely requires spatially aware controls (e.g., SSIM-guided constraints) rather than purely global concept suppression, as current approaches fail in this localized and semantically entangled setting.

title: Monitoring Post-Disaster Urban Recovery Using High-Resolution SAR Time Series and Unsupervised Learning: Evidence from the 2023 Türkiye-Syria Earthquake
comment: Submitted to IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing (JSTARS)
summary: Monitoring post-disaster recovery is essential for understanding how urban systems rebuild and progressively return to functionality. However, tracking reconstruction remains difficult because reliable ground-truth information is often scarce and recovery processes evolve over time. This paper proposes an unsupervised framework for recovery monitoring based on multi-temporal synthetic aperture radar (SAR) observations and deep-learning anomaly detection. COSMO-SkyMed time series are used to identify persistent temporal anomalies associated with reconstruction activities and to generate spatially explicit recovery maps. The framework is applied to four cities severely affected by the 2023 Turkiye-Syria earthquakes, revealing heterogeneous reconstruction dynamics across different urban contexts. The results show spatially structured patterns of persistent anomalies related to reconstruction over damaged and cleared areas, temporary container settlements, and new residential districts. Comparison with nighttime-light recovery indicators derived from SDGSAT-1 data highlights the complementary nature of the two modalities: nighttime lights reflect the restoration of electricity supply and nighttime socioeconomic activity, whereas SAR anomalies capture structural changes in the built environment and may reveal reconstruction at earlier stages. The results demonstrate that multi-temporal SAR data combined with unsupervised learning provide an effective and scalable approach for monitoring post-disaster reconstruction when labeled recovery datasets are unavailable.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an unsupervised framework using multi-temporal SAR and deep-learning anomaly detection to monitor post-disaster recovery. Applied to four cities affected by the 2023 Türkiye-Syria earthquakes, it reveals heterogeneous reconstruction dynamics and shows SAR anomalies complement nighttime-light indicators from SDGSAT-1.
AI.motivation: Monitoring post-disaster recovery is essential for understanding how urban systems rebuild, but reliable ground-truth information is scarce and recovery processes evolve over time, making tracking reconstruction difficult.
AI.method: An unsupervised framework combining multi-temporal COSMO-SkyMed SAR observations with deep-learning anomaly detection to identify persistent temporal anomalies associated with reconstruction activities and generate spatially explicit recovery maps.
AI.result: Applied to four cities from the 2023 Türkiye-Syria earthquakes, revealing spatially structured patterns of persistent anomalies over damaged/cleared areas, container settlements, and new residential districts. SAR anomalies and nighttime-light indicators (SDGSAT-1) are complementary: nighttime lights capture electricity restoration, while SAR captures structural changes earlier.
AI.conclusion: Multi-temporal SAR data combined with unsupervised learning provides an effective and scalable approach for monitoring post-disaster reconstruction when labeled recovery datasets are unavailable.

title: ACM: Agentic Context Management for Long Horizon Tasks
summary: Agentic tasks are inherently long-horizon and multi-turn, constantly accumulating context through interactions with the environment. Existing context compression methods inevitably incur information loss and are triggered by rigid heuristic rules, leaving them misaligned with the agent's evolving reasoning focus. We propose Agentic Context Management (ACM), a framework that equips agents with purpose-built context editing tools for lossless context management. Inspired by the interaction between short-term and long-term human memory, the agent autonomously decides when to compress its context, offloads discarded content to an external memory system, and queries it on demand for later retrieval. Building on this framework, we further develop a post-training pipeline that constructs high-quality demonstrations of context management and improves model performance on both agentic search and coding tasks. Further analysis reveals that effective context management reduces peak token pressure, enables extended explorations, and yields more consistent solutions across independent trials. Code, data, and model checkpoints are available at https://github.com/lixiaochuan2020/agentic-context-management.

AI.tldr: ACM proposes Agentic Context Management that equips agents with lossless context editing tools, inspired by human memory, allowing autonomous compression decisions, external memory offloading, and on-demand retrieval. A post-training pipeline improves agent performance on search and coding tasks.
AI.motivation: Existing context compression methods for long-horizon agentic tasks incur information loss and rely on rigid heuristic rules that misalign with the agent's evolving reasoning focus.
AI.method: A framework where agents autonomously decide when to compress context, offload discarded content to external memory, and query it on demand, inspired by short-term/long-term human memory interaction. Plus a post-training pipeline for constructing high-quality demonstrations.
AI.result: Effective context management reduces peak token pressure, enables extended explorations, and yields more consistent solutions across independent trials on agentic search and coding tasks.
AI.conclusion: Lossless, autonomous context management via external memory and purpose-built editing tools improves agent performance on long-horizon tasks compared to heuristic-based compression methods.

title: BeyondFusion: Self-Aligned Latent Diffusion for Calibration-Free Infrared Super-Resolution and Infrared-Visible Fusion
summary: Mobile infrared-visible imaging typically pairs a compact infrared sensor with a high-resolution visible camera for complementary perception. While cross-sensor misalignment caused by different optics, viewpoints, fields of view, and exposure timings hinders practical deployment. In this paper, we propose BeyondFusion, a unified latent diffusion framework for calibration-free visible-guided infrared super-resolution and infrared-visible fusion tasks. The proposed framework supports both task-specific training and joint training where two tasks are optimized and executed as two readouts of the same generative process. Instead of relying on explicit registration or geometric warping, BeyondFusion introduces a cross-modal self-aligning (CMSA) module into the denoising U-Net. CMSA reorganizes infrared and visible latent tokens into a shared attention space to learn content-adaptive cross-modal correspondence during the denoising process. Together with misalignment augmentation module, the model is facilitated to exploit visible structural and semantic cues while preserving thermal consistency, enabling high-frequency infrared reconstruction and informative fused-image generation under uncalibrated conditions. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks and a mobile infrared-visible imaging system show strong performance across aligned inputs, low-resolution infrared observations, synthetic misalignments, and real mobile captures with unsynchronized sensors. Ablation studies, unified training analysis, and downstream pedestrian detection further validate the effectiveness of BeyondFusion for calibration-free multimodal imaging.

AI.tldr: BeyondFusion is a unified latent diffusion framework for calibration-free visible-guided infrared super-resolution and infrared-visible fusion, using a cross-modal self-aligning (CMSA) module in the denoising U-Net to learn content-adaptive cross-modal correspondence without explicit registration.
AI.motivation: Mobile infrared-visible imaging suffers from cross-sensor misalignment (different optics, viewpoints, FOVs, exposure timings), hindering practical deployment. Existing methods rely on explicit registration or geometric warping, which is fragile under uncalibrated conditions.
AI.method: A unified latent diffusion framework with a cross-modal self-aligning (CMSA) module in the denoising U-Net that reorganizes infrared and visible latent tokens into a shared attention space for learning content-adaptive cross-modal correspondence, plus a misalignment augmentation module to handle uncalibrated inputs.
AI.result: Strong performance across aligned inputs, low-resolution IR observations, synthetic misalignments, and real mobile captures with unsynchronized sensors, validated on public benchmarks and a mobile IR-visible imaging system.
AI.conclusion: BeyondFusion enables effective calibration-free multimodal imaging, validated by ablation studies, unified training analysis, and downstream pedestrian detection tasks.

title: Every Client Is an Environment: Federated De-confounding for Spatio-Temporal Forecasting
summary: Federated learning has emerged as a promising paradigm for spatio-temporal forecasting (STF), enabling collaborative model training without sharing raw observations. Existing federated STF methods primarily regard cross-client heterogeneity as an optimization challenge and mitigate it through personalized approaches. However, such heterogeneity fundamentally stems from diverse \emph{environmental conditions}, and these methods capture environment-specific forecasting patterns, hardly generalizing under environmental shifts. Our key insight is that the environmental diversity across federated clients should be exploited, as they provide \emph{complementary observations of the same underlying spatio-temporal system}. Based on this insight, we propose \method, a novel federated de-confounding framework that \textbf{treats clients as distinct causal environments}. \method leverages the client heterogeneity as distributed environmental evidence and learns a global prototype codebook to capture shared environmental regimes. We further derive a theoretical federated de-confounding bound that is linearly controlled by the averaged confounding strength. Extensive experiments demonstrate that \method consistently outperforms federated baselines, while providing transferable, interpretable, and communication-efficient environmental representations.

AI.tldr: A federated de-confounding framework for spatio-temporal forecasting that treats client heterogeneity as diverse environmental evidence, learning a global prototype codebook to capture shared environmental regimes for better generalization under environmental shifts.
AI.motivation: Existing federated STF methods treat cross-client heterogeneity as an optimization challenge and mitigate it via personalization, but this captures environment-specific patterns that fail to generalize under environmental shifts. The authors aim to exploit environmental diversity across clients as complementary observations of the same underlying spatio-temporal system.
AI.method: Proposes a federated de-confounding framework called \method that treats clients as distinct causal environments, leverages client heterogeneity as distributed environmental evidence, learns a global prototype codebook to capture shared environmental regimes, and derives a theoretical federated de-confounding bound controlled by averaged confounding strength.
AI.result: Consistently outperforms federated baselines on extensive experiments, while providing transferable, interpretable, and communication-efficient environmental representations.
AI.conclusion: Client heterogeneity in federated STF should be exploited rather than mitigated; the proposed de-confounding approach yields better generalization under environmental shifts with additional benefits of transferability, interpretability, and communication efficiency.

title: Do Visual Features Improve Other-Initiated Repair Detection? A Dyadic Multimodal Approach
comment: Accepted to ICMI 2026 (International Conference on Multimodal Interaction), October 5-9, 2026, Napoli, Italy
summary: Other-initiated Self-repair, or in short Other-initiated Repair (OIR), is an essential mechanism in conversational interaction, whereby a recipient signals a problem in speaking, hearing, or understanding, prompting the previous speaker to resolve it. In the case of conversational agents, it is essential to accurately identify these repair initiation strategies to address communication breakdowns efficiently. While conversational analysis studies have shown that OIR initiation is accompanied by both verbal and non-verbal signals such as gaze shifts, facial expressions, body postures, and hand gestures, existing computational approaches rely mainly on text and audio. This paper introduces a novel multimodal model for OIR detection and classification, incorporating a set of visual features drawn from conversation analysis. We evaluate our approach on two corpora with distinct languages and interaction settings. Results demonstrate that visual information consistently improves performance over text and audio baselines, and provide insights into cross-modal feature contributions across two corpora.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a multimodal model for Other-initiated Repair (OIR) detection and classification that incorporates visual features from conversation analysis, improving performance over text and audio baselines on two corpora in different languages and settings.
AI.motivation: Existing computational approaches for OIR detection rely mainly on text and audio, ignoring non-verbal signals (gaze, facial expressions, body postures, hand gestures) that conversation analysis studies have shown to accompany repair initiation. The paper aims to close this gap by introducing a multimodal model that leverages visual features.
AI.method: The authors propose a novel multimodal model for OIR detection and classification that incorporates a set of visual features derived from conversation analysis, combined with text and audio modalities. The approach is evaluated on two corpora with distinct languages and interaction settings.
AI.result: Visual information consistently improves OIR detection and classification performance over text and audio baselines. Cross-modal feature contributions are analyzed across the two corpora, revealing insights into how different modalities contribute in different interaction settings and languages.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating visual features from conversation analysis enhances OIR detection in conversational agents, demonstrating the value of multimodal approaches for addressing communication breakdowns more efficiently.

title: ViDS: Video Diffusion Shader using 3D Face Tracking
comment: 12 pages, 6 figures, and 8 tables. Project page: https://fusheng-ji.github.io/ViDS/
summary: We introduce ViDS, a Video Diffusion Shader that leverages 3D face tracking for expressive and identity-preserving portrait animation. We first reconstruct the identity-specific 3DMM mesh from the reference image, and then animate it using expression and pose parameters from a driving video. Leveraging dense geometric cues from 3DMM normal maps, we employ a video diffusion model as a neural shader to synthesize lifelike portrait animations while preserving the appearance and identity of the reference image. We find that more accurate 3DMM tracking enables finer-grained expression control. We also introduce an autoregressive diffusion sampling process that extends generation beyond the model's native window while reducing discontinuities between adjacent clips. Compared with prior diffusion-based approaches for portrait animation that rely on landmark-based conditioning or implicit motion latents, our method achieves more detailed and consistent expression and pose control while faithfully preserving identity and appearance. Detailed ablation studies validate the effectiveness of our design choices. Project page: https://fusheng-ji.github.io/ViDS/

AI.tldr: ViDS is a video diffusion shader that uses 3D face tracking and 3DMM normal maps to animate portraits from a single reference image, achieving expressive, identity-preserving animation with fine-grained expression control and autoregressive long-video generation.
AI.motivation: Existing diffusion-based portrait animation methods rely on landmark-based conditioning or implicit motion latents, which lack fine-grained expression and pose control and often struggle with identity preservation.
AI.method: ViDS reconstructs an identity-specific 3DMM mesh from a reference image, animates it using expression/pose parameters from a driving video, renders dense 3DMM normal maps as geometric cues, and uses a video diffusion model as a neural shader to synthesize lifelike animations. An autoregressive diffusion sampling process extends generation beyond the model's native temporal window.
AI.result: The method achieves more detailed and consistent expression and pose control compared to prior landmark-based or implicit motion latent approaches, while faithfully preserving identity and appearance.
AI.conclusion: 3DMM-based geometric conditioning with video diffusion enables superior portrait animation quality. More accurate 3DMM tracking yields finer-grained expression control, and autoregressive sampling reduces discontinuities in long video generation.

title: Why does Greedy Search produce Optimal Clustering Outcomes? A Fixed-Core Assignment Theory
summary: Many existing clustering methods are designed based on a set-oriented definition---a cluster is a set of similar points---relying a point-to-point similarity function to find similar points. This works well for compact clusters, but clustering performance can deteriorate badly when cluster shapes are irregular, and densities or sizes vary between clusters. Recent `Cluster-as-Distribution' (CaD) clustering has been shown to discover these generic types of clusters in practice by treating each cluster as a set of independent and identically distributed points generated from some unknown distribution via a greedy search, achieving a clustering objective equivalent to that of Spectral Clustering, but with better clustering outcomes without eigen-decomposition. However, a theoretical analysis of this phenomenon is still lacking. Our analyses are from two angles. First, we analyze the approximation error between the true and empirical distribution embeddings. Second, we show that the greedy search employed to achieve the CaD clustering objective can be mapped to a partition matroid---yielding greedy optimality. These yield a near-optimality guarantee for the CaD clustering objective, with regret controlled by the approximation error. This is the first analysis that explains why CaD clustering via greedy search can discover clusters of arbitrary shapes, densities and sizes (where all set-oriented clustering methods have failed to discover) when the estimated cluster embeddings faithfully approximate the underlying cluster distributions.

AI.tldr: Cluster-as-Distribution (CaD) clustering is theoretically analyzed, showing that greedy search near-optimally discovers clusters of arbitrary shapes, densities, and sizes by treating each cluster as a distribution—explaining its advantage over set-oriented methods.
AI.motivation: Set-oriented clustering methods (e.g., point-to-point similarity) fail on irregular cluster shapes or varying densities/sizes. CaD clustering empirically outperforms them, but lacks theoretical justification.
AI.method: Two-angle analysis: (1) approximation error between true and empirical distribution embeddings; (2) mapping greedy search for CaD objective to a partition matroid, yielding greedy optimality.
AI.result: A near-optimality guarantee for CaD clustering objective is established, with regret bounded by the approximation error.
AI.conclusion: CaD clustering via greedy search can discover clusters of arbitrary shapes, densities, and sizes when distribution embeddings are faithful, marking the first theoretical explanation for its empirical success over set-oriented methods.

title: Understanding Human-like Solutions in Combinatorial Optimization via Learning and Search
summary: Humans often find good solutions to combinatorial optimization problems that are computationally hard even for advanced computer algorithms. In the Euclidean traveling salesman problems (TSP), people rapidly produce tours that are near-optimal, despite severe limits on time and computation. What makes a tour human-like, and how might such solutions be learned? Here we address these questions through a large-scale behavioral and computational investigation of human performance in Euclidean TSP. We sampled a broad space of TSP instances, collected human solutions, and compared them with neural policies based on Pointer Networks, which are recurrent neural networks with an attention-based pointing mechanism that define probability distributions over valid tours. We trained these networks under multiple objectives, including reinforcement learning (RL), supervised learning from optimal tours, supervised learning from human tours, and RL fine-tuning after optimal-supervised pretraining. Human tours were not identical to optimal tours, but occupied a near-optimal geometric basin: they shared many structural properties with optimal solutions while preserving systematic human-specific deviations. The best account of human tours was not direct imitation of optimal tours, but a model pretrained on optimal tours, fine-tuned by RL, and decoded through $\text{Best-of-}N$ sampling. These findings suggest that human-like solutions may emerge from a combination of structured supervised learning, RL, and test-time search, echoing computational principles underlying many modern artificial intelligence systems.

AI.tldr: Humans produce near-optimal tours in Euclidean TSP, and the best computational model for human-like solutions is a Pointer Network pretrained on optimal tours, fine-tuned via reinforcement learning, and decoded with Best-of-N sampling.
AI.motivation: To understand what makes a tour human-like and how human-like solutions to hard combinatorial optimization problems (Euclidean TSP) can be learned, given that humans rapidly produce near-optimal solutions despite computational limits.
AI.method: Large-scale behavioral experiment collecting human solutions across diverse TSP instances; trained Pointer Networks (RNNs with attention-based pointing) under multiple objectives: reinforcement learning (RL), supervised learning from optimal tours, supervised learning from human tours, and RL fine-tuning after optimal-supervised pretraining.
AI.result: Human tours are near-optimal, sharing structural properties with optimal solutions but with systematic deviations. The best model for human tours was pretrained on optimal tours, fine-tuned by RL, and decoded through Best-of-N sampling, outperforming direct imitation of optimal tours.
AI.conclusion: Human-like solutions emerge from combining structured supervised learning, RL, and test-time search, mirroring computational principles in modern AI systems.

title: LoTA-N2N: Local Trace Adaptation for Zero-Shot Self-Supervised Image Denoising
summary: Single-image self-supervised denoising replaces unavailable clean targets with surrogate targets constructed from noisy observations. Its effectiveness therefore depends on how closely the surrogate objective remains aligned with supervised denoising, especially when noise is correlated, spatially nonstationary, or unknown. We express the discrepancy between a broad class of MSE-based self-supervised objectives and supervised MSE as a parameter-independent constant and a trace interaction between the surrogate-target residual and the prediction error. The corresponding gradient discrepancy is determined by the gradient of this interaction. This formulation provides a common view of paired-noise, blind-spot, weak-noise, re-corruption, and sub-image methods, while revealing that a small global interaction may conceal substantial positive and negative regional interactions through spatial cancellation. Building on these observations, we propose LoTA-N2N, a two-stage zero-shot adaptation framework. Stage 1 trains a denoiser on complementary sub-image pairs and freezes it to construct detached clean-sub-image proxies. Stage 2 estimates the residual--prediction interaction using these proxies and suppresses its patch-wise absolute magnitude. We show that the local construction prevents spatial cancellation and upper-bounds the magnitude of the corresponding global interaction. Experiments across natural, confocal, and X-ray images, complemented by iteration-matched controls, controlled noise shifts, and gradient diagnostics, show consistent gains over MSE-only adaptation under IID, spatially varying, and mixed noise. Overall, LoTA-N2N demonstrates that estimated local interaction and spatial cancellation control provide effective design principles for single-image self-supervised denoising without paired clean targets, repeated acquisitions, or a predefined re-corruption model.

AI.tldr: LoTA-N2N is a two-stage zero-shot self-supervised denoising framework that estimates and suppresses local residual-prediction interactions to avoid spatial cancellation, achieving consistent gains over MSE-only adaptation under various noise types.
AI.motivation: Single-image self-supervised denoising suffers from a discrepancy between surrogate and supervised objectives, especially under correlated, nonstationary, or unknown noise. The paper identifies that spatial cancellation of residual-prediction interactions can conceal substantial regional errors, motivating the need for local interaction suppression.
AI.method: The paper first formulates the discrepancy between MSE-based self-supervised and supervised objectives as a constant plus a trace interaction between surrogate-target residual and prediction error. Then proposes LoTA-N2N: Stage 1 trains a denoiser on complementary sub-image pairs and freezes it to build clean-sub-image proxies; Stage 2 estimates the residual-prediction interaction from these proxies and suppresses its patch-wise absolute magnitude, preventing spatial cancellation.
AI.result: Experiments on natural, confocal, and X-ray images with iteration-matched controls, controlled noise shifts, and gradient diagnostics show consistent improvements over MSE-only adaptation under IID, spatially varying, and mixed noise.
AI.conclusion: Estimated local interaction and spatial cancellation control are effective design principles for single-image self-supervised denoising without paired clean targets, repeated acquisitions, or predefined re-corruption models.

title: ML-based Predictive Models for Power Consumption in Virtualised O-RANs
summary: As communication networks adopt virtualized and disaggregated architectures, achieving energy efficiency has become increasingly important for both economic and environmental reasons. Traditional methods for power modeling are inadequate in these dynamic software-defined environments due to their inability to model complex and nonlinear factors affecting energy use. We investigate the use of feature extraction and regressor-based machine learning methods for predicting power consumption in virtualized open radio access networks (O-RANs), utilizing datasets from a hardware-instrumented testbed. We test three variants of deep neural networks (DNNs), namely, a standard DNN, a regularized DNN, and a hybrid model combining DNN-based feature extraction with an XGBoost regressor. We evaluate the performance of these models for various system parameters such as transmission gain, modulation/coding schemes, and airtime. We show that the hybrid model consistently outperformed others, achieving a mean relative error below 0.5%. Results suggest hybrid models like DNN-XGBoost offer superior accuracy and could be integrated into O-RAN management tools to enable more energy-efficient network orchestration in future networks.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes hybrid DNN-XGBoost models for predicting power consumption in virtualized O-RANs, achieving <0.5% mean relative error, outperforming standard and regularized DNNs.
AI.motivation: Traditional power modeling methods fail in dynamic software-defined virtualized network environments like O-RAN due to their inability to capture complex nonlinear energy consumption factors.
AI.method: The authors implement three DNN variants (standard, regularized, hybrid DNN-XGBoost) using feature extraction and regression-based ML, trained on data from a hardware-instrumented testbed with parameters including transmission gain, modulation/coding schemes, and airtime.
AI.result: The hybrid DNN-XGBoost model consistently outperforms both standard and regularized DNNs, achieving a mean relative error below 0.5%.
AI.conclusion: Hybrid models like DNN-XGBoost offer superior power prediction accuracy and could be integrated into O-RAN management tools to enable more energy-efficient network orchestration.

title: Cost-Aware Recovery-Pathway Identification and Bayesian Optimization for Autonomous Materials Discovery
summary: Autonomous laboratories automate experimental execution, but a campaign must also decide which recovery pathway merits optimization. We formulate this as a sequential decision problem with a discrete pathway-identification stage and a continuous within-pathway optimization stage under heterogeneous experimental costs. Our implementation, Coactive learning, combines a cost-sensitive Bayesian hypothesis-discrimination policy motivated by EC2 (Golovin et al., 2010) with Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization (Srinivas et al., 2010). Under explicitly stated assumptions, the expected spend of one fixed-budget campaign attempt is bounded by the expected pathway-identification cost plus the capped within-pathway optimization budget. We evaluate the method on synthetic benchmarks constrained by selected results reported for PNNL's CICERO selective-precipitation study (Ritchhart et al., 2026). The method performs comparably to an oracle-pathway Bayesian-optimization reference and to a strong split-plate baseline that discriminates pathways with its first plate, without receiving an oracle label for the correct pathway. It is given a candidate hypothesis space and a diagnostic likelihood model. On an NdFeB-inspired instance, it avoids the simulated penalty of a commit-first baseline that initially selects a plausible but inferior hydroxide pathway. This hypothetical wrong-first-commitment scenario is motivated by the hydroxide-oxalate performance contrast reported by CICERO. We characterize the sensitivity of these conclusions to the assumed cost model. The code and benchmark are open source.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces Coactive learning, a method combining cost-sensitive Bayesian hypothesis discrimination with Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization for autonomous laboratories. It handles both discrete pathway identification and continuous within-pathway optimization under heterogeneous costs, demonstrating comparable performance to oracle methods and avoiding costly wrong-first commitments.
AI.motivation: Autonomous laboratories need to decide not only how to optimize within a chosen experimental pathway, but also which recovery pathway to pursue in the first place. This dual decision problem under heterogeneous experimental costs lacks a principled formulation.
AI.method: The problem is formulated as a sequential decision problem with two stages: discrete pathway identification (using a cost-sensitive Bayesian hypothesis-discrimination policy motivated by EC2) and continuous within-pathway optimization (using Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization). The combined approach is called Coactive learning.
AI.result: The method performs comparably to an oracle-pathway Bayesian-optimization reference and a strong split-plate baseline on synthetic benchmarks based on PNNL's CICERO selective-precipitation study. On an NdFeB-inspired instance, it avoids the penalty of a commit-first baseline that wrongly selects an inferior hydroxide pathway.
AI.conclusion: Coactive learning provides a principled framework for autonomous experimental campaigns with discrete pathway choices and heterogeneous costs, with bounded expected spend. The sensitivity of conclusions to the assumed cost model is characterized, and all code and benchmarks are open source.

title: Image Inpainting via Stochastic Dynamics
summary: Image inpainting aims to recover missing regions while preserving structural consistency. We propose a non-parametric method without network training based on data-guided stochastic dynamics. Starting from a masked image, the missing pixels are evolved through a reverse-time stochastic differential equation with a kernel-weighted correction estimated directly from a reference dataset. This empirical correction guides the reconstruction toward high-density regions of the data distribution without training a neural network or fitting a parametric density model. Experiments on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and MVTec show that the proposed method outperforms Mean Fill, Telea, and Navier-Stokes inpainting in PSNR, SSIM, and visual quality. On CelebA, it remains competitive and produces plausible completions for structure-sensitive occlusions. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of empirical reference statistics as a non-parametric prior for image inpainting.

AI.tldr: A non-parametric image inpainting method using reverse-time SDEs with kernel-weighted corrections from a reference dataset, requiring no neural network training.
AI.motivation: To recover missing image regions while preserving structural consistency without the need for network training or parametric density modeling.
AI.method: Uses a reverse-time stochastic differential equation (SDE) with a kernel-weighted correction estimated directly from a reference dataset to evolve missing pixels toward high-density regions of the data distribution.
AI.result: Outperforms Mean Fill, Telea, and Navier-Stokes inpainting on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and MVTec in PSNR, SSIM, and visual quality; competitive on CelebA.
AI.conclusion: Empirical reference statistics serve as an effective non-parametric prior for image inpainting, eliminating the need for trained models.

title: KAP: Bridging the Knowledge Selection-Runtime Consumption Gap in LLM Systems
summary: Modern LLM systems increasingly rely on knowledge-selection processes that produce high-value structured priors, such as ranked evidence, graph topology, multimodal alignment, and confidence signals. Yet LLM serving remains fundamentally oblivious to this rich structure: once such signals are serialized into a prompt, the backend observes only a flat token sequence, forcing dense and uniform consumption of the full key-value (KV) state during decoding. We term this architectural mismatch the Knowledge Selection-Runtime Consumption (KSRC) gap: richer contexts enlarge the full-prompt KV footprint and decode-time memory traffic, increasing latency and degrading throughput even when reasoning depends on only a small fraction of the context. To bridge the gap, we propose Knowledge Access Planning (KAP), a paradigm-shifting execution abstraction that elevates structured knowledge priors from passive prompt-construction hints into first-class physical execution artifacts. KAP establishes a universal intermediate representation (IR)-the runtime access plan-which compiles structured knowledge signals to govern physical KV access without altering logical prompt semantics, model weights, or training procedures. Through this IR, KAP shifts LLM serving from token-aware context consumption to plan-driven, knowledge-aware runtime consumption. We instantiate KAP with GraphSpec, a compiler-executor realization connecting structured knowledge selection to an LLM serving backend. We derive a phase-boundary model for the positive-speedup regime of plan-guided execution. Across 4K-128K long-context QA workloads, GraphSpec maintains answer quality comparable to full-context decoding while decoupling physical KV consumption from prompt length, reducing proposal-time KV access to 5.5% of source KV state at 128K, and fundamentally shifting the scaling trajectory of long-context generation.

AI.tldr: LLM serving is oblivious to structured knowledge priors (ranked evidence, graph topology, etc.), forcing uniform KV-state consumption. The paper proposes KAP, a paradigm that compiles these priors into runtime access plans to guide physical KV access, and instantiates it as GraphSpec, which decouples KV consumption from prompt length and reduces proposal-time KV access to 5.5% at 128K context.
AI.motivation: The KSRC gap: LLM backends treat all structured priors as flat token sequences, causing dense uniform KV consumption during decoding even when reasoning depends on only a small fraction of the context. This enlarges latency and degrades throughput as contexts grow richer.
AI.method: KAP introduces a universal IR (runtime access plan) that compiles structured knowledge signals to govern physical KV access without altering prompt semantics, model weights, or training. GraphSpec is a concrete compiler-executor realization connecting knowledge selection to the serving backend, with a phase-boundary model for speedup regimes.
AI.result: GraphSpec maintains answer quality comparable to full-context decoding across 4K-128K long-context QA, reduces proposal-time KV access to 5.5% of source KV state at 128K, and fundamentally shifts the scaling trajectory of long-context generation.
AI.conclusion: KAP bridges the KSRC gap by elevating structured knowledge priors from passive prompt hints to first-class execution artifacts, enabling plan-driven, knowledge-aware runtime consumption that decouples physical KV consumption from prompt length.

title: GOTS: Greedy Orthogonal Token Selection for High-Resolution Vision-Language Models
summary: Modern vision-language models (VLMs) increasingly rely on dynamic or high-resolution visual encoding, producing thousands of visual tokens that substantially increase downstream language-model inference cost. Existing token-reduction methods assess token utility through token-wise importance, query relevance, coverage, pairwise diversity, or subset-level objectives. Our key insight is to view visual token reduction through selected-span complementarity: instead of scoring a token in isolation or through pairwise relations, we assess how much of its feature is orthogonal to the span of the already retained subset. Based on this perspective, we propose Greedy Orthogonal Token Selection (GOTS), a training-free and query-agnostic method. At each step, GOTS selects the token with the largest residual energy orthogonal to the current retained span. This rule exactly maximizes the one-step augmented Gram determinant among candidate additions, giving each greedy step a precise local geometric guarantee for subset expansion. Across five high-resolution VLM backbones from the Qwen-VL and InternVL families and eleven diverse benchmarks, GOTS achieves higher average performance retention than the strongest evaluated baselines, and a controlled OCRBench study shows that it reduces model-side time-to-first-token after accounting for selection overhead. Code is available at https://github.com/newLLing/GOTS.

AI.tldr: GOTS is a training-free, query-agnostic visual token reduction method for VLMs that greedily selects tokens with maximal residual energy orthogonal to the current retained span, maximizing the Gram determinant at each step for precise local geometric guarantee. It outperforms baselines across five high-resolution VLM backbones and eleven benchmarks while reducing time-to-first-token.
AI.motivation: High-resolution VLMs produce thousands of visual tokens, increasing language-model inference cost. Existing token-reduction methods rely on token-wise importance, query relevance, diversity, or pairwise relations, lacking a principled geometric approach to complementarity among selected tokens.
AI.method: Greedy Orthogonal Token Selection (GOTS) selects tokens greedily based on the largest residual energy orthogonal to the span of already retained tokens, which exactly maximizes the one-step augmented Gram determinant for local geometric optimality. It is training-free and query-agnostic.
AI.result: GOTS achieves higher average performance retention than the strongest baselines across five VLM backbones (Qwen-VL and InternVL families) and eleven diverse benchmarks. A controlled OCRBench study shows it reduces model-side time-to-first-token after accounting for selection overhead.
AI.conclusion: Viewing visual token reduction through selected-span complementarity with orthogonal residual energy maximization provides a principled and effective approach, backed by a precise geometric guarantee at each greedy step, outperforming existing methods.

title: UniGen-AR: Unifying Visual Generation with Auto-Regressive Modeling
summary: Modern computer vision pipelines remain fragmented, with tasks such as text-to-image generation, editing, restoration, and classical perception handled by separate models. We study Unified Visual Generation (UVG), where a single model produces diverse image-valued outputs through a unified multimodal interface. While diffusion-based systems dominate UVG due to strong quality and controllability, their iterative sampling incurs substantial inference latency, limiting practical deployment. To address these limitations, we propose UniGen-AR, a framework that pairs a general-purpose multi-modal language model (MLLM) with an efficient next-scale visual auto-regressive (VAR) decoder. This design retains the flexibility of MLLM-based conditioning while leveraging the sampling efficiency and latent unification properties of VAR models. In our framework, the MLLM encodes free-form instructions and control signals into a unified sequence, which guides the VAR decoder to generate image-valued outputs for over 15 tasks spanning four families. Empirically, UniGen-AR achieves up to $19 \times$ lower inference latency than diffusion-based baselines while maintaining or improving output quality. Our ablations further reveal that VQ-VAE tokenizer design, particularly codebook size and hierarchy, is a critical factor for VAR scalability in UVG. These results establish visual auto-regressive modeling as a compelling and efficient backbone for unified visual generation. Our project page is at https://zpbao.github.io/projects/unigenar.

AI.tldr: UniGen-AR pairs an MLLM with a next-scale visual auto-regressive (VAR) decoder to achieve unified visual generation across 15+ tasks with up to 19× lower inference latency than diffusion models while maintaining quality.
AI.motivation: Current computer vision pipelines use separate models for different tasks (generation, editing, restoration, perception), leading to fragmentation. Diffusion-based unified models suffer from high inference latency due to iterative sampling, limiting practical deployment.
AI.method: UniGen-AR combines a general-purpose MLLM for encoding free-form instructions and control signals into a unified sequence, paired with an efficient next-scale visual auto-regressive (VAR) decoder that leverages sampling efficiency and latent unification properties.
AI.result: Achieves up to 19× lower inference latency than diffusion-based baselines while maintaining or improving output quality across 15+ tasks. Ablations show VQ-VAE tokenizer design (codebook size and hierarchy) is critical for VAR scalability in UVG.
AI.conclusion: Visual auto-regressive modeling is a compelling and efficient backbone for unified visual generation, offering substantial latency improvements over diffusion-based approaches without sacrificing quality.

title: Physics-Guided Generative AI for Property-Targeted 3D Porous Media Design
summary: Inverse design of three-dimensional porous media is central to applications in filtration, catalysis, energy storage, fuel cells, thermal management, and biomedical scaffolds, but remains challenging because many distinct pore geometries can share similar porosity or permeability while small structural changes can strongly affect transport behaviour. This paper proposes a physics-guided generative AI framework for property-targeted porous media design, combining a property-aware variational autoencoder, a conditional latent diffusion model, and an independently trained differentiable structure-to-property surrogate. The framework learns a compact, physically informative latent design space, generates porous structures conditioned on target porosity and directional permeability, and refines generated samples using property-level feedback during denoising and decoding. Experiments on procedurally generated structures and real micro-CT porous-media datasets show improved target-property matching, directional permeability control, and property correlation compared with representative property-aware variational-autoencoder and latent-diffusion baselines. The results demonstrate a scalable route towards controllable inverse design of complex porous geometries and establish a foundation for simulation-informed generative AI tools in engineering and advanced materials discovery.

AI.tldr: A physics-guided generative AI framework (property-aware VAE + conditional latent diffusion + differentiable surrogate) for inverse design of 3D porous media with targeted porosity and directional permeability, outperforming baseline methods on synthetic and real micro-CT datasets.
AI.motivation: Inverse design of 3D porous media is important for many applications (filtration, catalysis, energy storage, etc.) but is challenging because different pore geometries can share similar bulk properties (porosity/permeability) while small structural changes strongly affect transport behavior.
AI.method: Proposes a three-component framework: (1) a property-aware variational autoencoder (VAE) that learns a physically informative latent space; (2) a conditional latent diffusion model that generates latent codes conditioned on target porosity and directional permeability; (3) an independently trained differentiable structure-to-property surrogate that provides property-level feedback during denoising and decoding.
AI.result: On procedurally generated structures and real micro-CT porous-media datasets, the method achieves improved target-property matching, directional permeability control, and property correlation compared to property-aware VAE and latent-diffusion baselines.
AI.conclusion: Demonstrates a scalable route towards controllable inverse design of complex porous geometries and establishes a foundation for simulation-informed generative AI in engineering and advanced materials discovery.

title: Reality Monitoring in Large Language Models: Self-Knowledge That Transforms with Conversation Memory
summary: A conversational AI that cannot tell its own output from what a user said will treat its own mistakes as user-provided facts. In humans, this capacity is called reality monitoring, and its failures are linked to hallucinations, delusions, and confabulation, yet whether LLMs possess it remains untested. Here we show, across two experiments and six LLMs, that source attribution depends on how conversational memory is structured: ceiling accuracy for self-generated content under minimal memory demands reverses to a fragile external-item advantage once episodic delay removes that shortcut. Feedback exposes two failures: in some models, internal and external judgments swap; in others, accuracy improves while confidence decouples from correctness, dissociations invisible to existing benchmarks. Across models, this pattern implicates active, not aggregate, parameter count. This suggests that as AI systems take on autonomous, multi-turn roles, evaluating what they know is not enough: tracking where that knowledge came from may matter equally.

AI.tldr: LLMs lack robust reality monitoring: they show ceiling accuracy for self-generated content under minimal memory load but this reverses under episodic delay, with some models swapping internal/external judgments and others decoupling confidence from correctness, a problem linked to active (not aggregate) parameter count.
AI.motivation: To test whether LLMs possess reality monitoring—the ability to distinguish self-generated output from user-provided input—a capacity whose failure in humans is linked to hallucinations and confabulation, and which remains untested in AI systems.
AI.method: Conducted two experiments across six LLMs, manipulating conversational memory structure (minimal memory demands vs. episodic delay) and measuring source attribution accuracy, confidence, and the dissociation between internal and external judgments.
AI.result: Ceiling accuracy for self-generated content under minimal memory reversed to a fragile external-item advantage under episodic delay; feedback revealed two failure modes: judgment swapping in some models, and accuracy-improvement-with-confidence-decoupling in others—dissociations invisible to standard benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Evaluating what AI systems know is insufficient; tracking the source of that knowledge is equally important as they take on autonomous, multi-turn roles, and this capacity depends on active parameter count rather than total parameters.

title: Do Current Retrievers Cover All the Evidence? A Controlled Study of Conjunctive Cross-Page Retrieval
summary: Finding a long document relevant to a multi-part request is not the same as establishing that it contains every requested piece of evidence. We study this gap for conjunctive document retrieval, where two or three explicit conditions must be supported on different pages of one document. We use n-Clue as a controlled measurement instrument: 1{,}000 queries over 2{,}021 documents pair all-condition golds with naturally occurring documents that satisfy only a subset, and a complete-first success requires a top-10 gold to precede every released subset qrel. Across 70 configurations, condition-wise decomposition improves two dense backbones by 6.8--7.3 points and lexical--visual fusion adds 8.7, while four generic rerankers all reduce Gold-NDCG; these directions replicate on a four-source stress set. Scaling one dense family from 0.6B to 8B changes complete-first success by 0.0 points. The strongest displayed hybrid illustrates the resulting gap: it finds a gold for 81.1\% of queries but succeeds complete-first on only 35.8\%, and the gap persists across condition count, target length, candidate density, query rendering, and the four-source stress set. Finally, page-aware visual systems surface stored support for every condition on only 5.1--5.3\% of queries. These results identify condition coverage, rather than gold discovery alone, as the central bottleneck.

AI.tldr: This paper studies conjunctive document retrieval where multiple conditions must be satisfied across different pages of a single document. Using n-Clue with 1,000 queries and 2,021 documents, the authors find that condition-wise decomposition improves dense retrieval by 6.8-7.3 points and lexical-visual fusion adds 8.7 points, while scaling models from 0.6B to 8B parameters yields no improvement. The strongest hybrid finds gold documents for 81.1% of queries but succeeds complete-first on only 35.8%, revealing condition coverage as the central bottleneck.
AI.motivation: Standard document retrieval evaluates relevance at the document level, but multi-part requests require verifying that every condition is explicitly supported within the document. This gap between finding a relevant document and confirming it contains all requested evidence is understudied.
AI.method: The authors construct n-Clue, a controlled benchmark of 1,000 queries over 2,021 documents with conjunctive conditions (2-3 conditions), pairing all-condition golds with documents satisfying only subsets. They evaluate 70 configurations including dense retrievers (0.6B-8B), lexical-visual fusion, and generic rerankers under a complete-first success metric requiring top-10 gold to precede every released subset qrel.
AI.result: Condition-wise decomposition improves dense backbones by 6.8-7.3 points; lexical-visual fusion adds 8.7 points; scaling dense models from 0.6B to 8B yields 0.0 point improvement; generic rerankers all reduce Gold-NDCG; strongest hybrid finds golds for 81.1% of queries but succeeds complete-first on only 35.8%; page-aware visual systems surface support for all conditions on only 5.1-5.3% of queries.
AI.conclusion: The central bottleneck in conjunctive document retrieval is condition coverage—ensuring every requested condition is supported in the retrieved document—rather than gold discovery alone. Current systems fail to bridge this gap, and scaling model size does not address it.

title: MEGA-CL: A Molecular Foundation Model for Generalizable ADMET Prediction through Graph External Attention and Contrastive Learning
summary: Predicting the absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion and toxicity (ADMET) properties of small molecules remains a major challenge in drug discovery. Here, we present MEGA-CL, a foundation graph neural network framework for universal molecular ADMET prediction. MEGA-CL integrates self-supervised contrastive learning with a multi-head external attention mechanism and an enhanced message-passing architecture, enabling simultaneous modeling of local chemical substructures and global inter-graph relationships while mitigating over-smoothing effects commonly observed in deep graph networks. Across 13 benchmark datasets and 21 downstream ADMET tasks, MEGA-CL consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baseline models. In particular, the framework demonstrates robust performance on challenging regression tasks, including clearance (CL) and steady-state volume of distribution (VDss), while maintaining strong generalization ability in independent external validation. Clinically relevant predictive accuracy was achieved, with more than 75% of predictions falling within a 3-fold error range. In an external evaluation on 18 novel compounds derived from recently approved FDA drugs, over 50% of human liver microsome clearance (HLMC) predictions were within a 2-fold error range. To further assess its practical applicability, MEGA-CL was prospectively evaluated on three preclinical drug candidates using in vitro hepatic microsomal metabolism assays and CYP450 inhibition assays guided by model predictions. The predicted HLMC values for all candidates were within 2.5-fold of the experimentally measured values, and 73.3% of CYP450 inhibition endpoints (11/15) were correctly classified. These results demonstrate the potential of MEGA-CL as a generalizable framework for accelerating in silico ADMET evaluation and early-stage drug candidate optimization.

AI.tldr: MEGA-CL is a graph neural network framework integrating contrastive learning with multi-head external attention and enhanced message passing for universal ADMET prediction, outperforming baselines across 21 downstream tasks and demonstrating strong generalization on external validation, FDA-derived compounds, and preclinical drug candidates.
AI.motivation: Predicting ADMET properties of small molecules remains a major challenge in drug discovery, limiting the efficiency of early-stage candidate optimization.
AI.method: MEGA-CL combines self-supervised contrastive learning, a multi-head external attention mechanism, and an enhanced message-passing architecture to model local chemical substructures and global inter-graph relationships while mitigating over-smoothing in deep graph networks.
AI.result: Outperforms state-of-the-art models across 13 benchmark datasets and 21 ADMET tasks; >75% of predictions within 3-fold error; >50% of HLMC predictions within 2-fold error on 18 FDA-derived compounds; HLMC within 2.5-fold for all 3 preclinical candidates; 73.3% CYP450 inhibition endpoints correctly classified.
AI.conclusion: MEGA-CL is a generalizable framework that can accelerate in silico ADMET evaluation and early-stage drug candidate optimization.

title: MemTX: Transactional Belief Commit for Stateful Agent Memory
summary: LLM agents increasingly coordinate through persistent shared memory: one agent's write becomes another agent's premise, and eventually a tool call with real side effects. Current agent memory systems treat every accepted write as immediately actionable truth, so a polluted tool result, a stale update, or a teammate's half-finished note can silently drive an irreversible action. We argue that a memory write is not a belief commit. We present MemTX, a transactional belief-commit protocol. Each record carries evidence, permissions, provenance, and validity. Writes are staged inside snapshot-isolated transactions and admitted by a validate-and-commit pipeline, irreversible tool calls are gated on in-flight belief state, and retracting a belief triggers typed cascading repair of its derived records and tool side effects. Two invariants, action-safety gating and cascade-repair completeness, are machine-checked by property-based testing and bounded exhaustive enumeration of 5.5 million protocol states, with zero violations. Across five backbones from three model families, MemTX leads all eight baselines with paired-McNemar significance on four backbones and statistically ties the best baseline on the fifth and strongest, while remaining the only method with zero downstream harm on every backbone. Backbone capability does not substitute for commit discipline.

AI.tldr: MemTX is a transactional belief-commit protocol for LLM agent memory systems that prevents harmful irreversible actions by staging writes in snapshot-isolated transactions with validation pipelines, evidence tracking, and cascading repair, achieving zero safety violations across 5.5M protocol states and outperforming all baselines across five backbones.
AI.motivation: Current LLM agent memory systems treat every accepted write as immediately actionable truth, causing polluted tool results, stale updates, or incomplete notes to silently drive irreversible actions with real-world side effects.
AI.method: MemTX implements a transactional belief-commit protocol where each record carries evidence, permissions, provenance, and validity. Writes are staged in snapshot-isolated transactions, admitted via a validate-and-commit pipeline, irreversible tool calls are gated on in-flight belief state, and retracting a belief triggers typed cascading repair of derived records and tool side effects. Two invariants (action-safety gating and cascade-repair completeness) are machine-checked via property-based testing and bounded exhaustive enumeration of 5.5M protocol states.
AI.result: Across five backbones from three model families, MemTX leads all eight baselines with paired-McNemar significance on four backbones and statistically ties the best baseline on the fifth (strongest) backbone. It remains the only method with zero downstream harm on every backbone.
AI.conclusion: Backbone capability does not substitute for commit discipline. The transactional protocol is essential for safe LLM agent coordination.

title: LCMamNet: A Lightweight Cross-scale Mamba Network for Infrared Small Target Detection
summary: Infrared small target detection (IRSTD) is important for low-altitude perception, unmanned-system warning, and security monitoring. However, weak targets in infrared imagery usually occupy only a few pixels and are easily submerged by cloud clutter, ground edges, and bright noise, making it difficult for lightweight segmentation-based methods to preserve local target structures while suppressing background interference. To address these challenges, we propose LCMamNet, a lightweight cross-scale Mamba network that progressively enhances local target structures, interacts cross-scale context in a latent space, and restores spatial details with background suppression. Specifically, a compact hierarchical encoder with cross-shaped directional bottleneck residual (CDBR) blocks strengthens direction-sensitive target structures under a small computation budget. A latent dense cross-scale fusion (LDCF) module then performs dense all-level interaction through bidirectional Mamba modeling and reorganizes the interacted features into stable hierarchical semantics. Finally, a progressive decoder selectively recovers shallow spatial details while suppressing irrelevant background textures. Extensive experiments on IRSTD-1k, NUAA-SIRST, and NUDT-SIRST show that the proposed network achieves mIoU scores of 71.25\%, 79.60\%, and 95.58\%, respectively, with only 1.175M parameters and 6.91 GFLOPs. It also runs with a mean inference latency of 6.62 ms, and deployment results on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX 16G SUPER further demonstrate its practical potential for real-time edge inference. The code and checkpoints are publicly available at https://github.com/Haoyu096/LCMamNet.

AI.tldr: LCMamNet is a lightweight cross-scale Mamba network for infrared small target detection that uses a compact hierarchical encoder with CDBR blocks, a latent dense cross-scale fusion module, and a progressive decoder to achieve state-of-the-art performance (71.25%-95.58% mIoU) with only 1.175M parameters and 6.91 GFLOPs, enabling real-time edge inference on platforms like NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX.
AI.motivation: Infrared small target detection faces challenges because weak targets occupy only a few pixels and are easily submerged by cloud clutter, ground edges, and bright noise. Lightweight segmentation-based methods struggle to preserve local target structures while suppressing background interference.
AI.method: The proposed LCMamNet consists of three key components: (1) a compact hierarchical encoder with cross-shaped directional bottleneck residual (CDBR) blocks that enhance direction-sensitive target structures with low computation; (2) a latent dense cross-scale fusion (LDCF) module that performs dense all-level interaction via bidirectional Mamba modeling and reorganizes features into stable hierarchical semantics; (3) a progressive decoder that selectively recovers shallow spatial details while suppressing irrelevant background textures.
AI.result: On IRSTD-1k, NUAA-SIRST, and NUDT-SIRST datasets, LCMamNet achieves mIoU scores of 71.25%, 79.60%, and 95.58% respectively, with only 1.175M parameters and 6.91 GFLOPs, and a mean inference latency of 6.62 ms.
AI.conclusion: The proposed LCMamNet achieves effective infrared small target detection with extremely lightweight architecture, demonstrating practical potential for real-time edge inference on platforms like NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX 16G SUPER.

title: DynaCalKV: Key-Value Cache Compression via Head Grouping and Adaptive Rank Allocation
summary: As the inference phase of Large Language Models (LLMs) requires handling long context windows, the Key-Value (KV) cache initially appears to address this challenge but eventually becomes a significant bottleneck as the context window continues to grow. Low-rank compression has recently been studied as an effective approach to reduce KV cache memory while maintaining model performance. However, only a few existing methods treat the Key and Value caches differently, despite their distinct roles. Moreover, these methods typically employ fixed attention-head grouping, which may not fully exploit the structural similarity among attention heads. In this paper, we propose an improved low-rank KV cache compression framework. For the Key cache, we dynamically group attention heads based on Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) similarity and allocate the rank budget adaptively under a parameter budget. For the Value cache, we adopt the same approach as ReCalKV, refining the low-rank decomposition through offline calibration to improve reconstruction quality. Experimental results on three instruction-tuned LLMs show that our method reduces the number of Key cache parameters while maintaining competitive accuracy. We further observe that the proposed strategy is particularly effective for Multi-Head Attention (MHA) models, whereas it should be applied more conservatively to Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) models, especially in long-context settings.

AI.tldr: Proposes an improved low-rank KV cache compression framework that dynamically groups Key cache attention heads via CKA similarity and adaptively allocates rank budgets, while using offline-calibrated low-rank decomposition for Value cache (similar to ReCalKV). Shows effectiveness on MHA models but advises conservative application for GQA models in long-context settings.
AI.motivation: KV cache becomes a bottleneck as LLM context windows grow; existing low-rank compression methods treat Key and Value caches similarly despite their distinct roles and use fixed attention-head grouping that fails to exploit structural similarity among heads.
AI.method: (1) For Key cache: dynamic grouping of attention heads based on CKA similarity, with adaptive rank budget allocation under a parameter budget. (2) For Value cache: low-rank decomposition refined via offline calibration (following ReCalKV).
AI.result: Reduces Key cache parameters while maintaining competitive accuracy on three instruction-tuned LLMs. Particularly effective for MHA models; requires more conservative application for GQA models, especially in long-context settings.
AI.conclusion: Dynamic CKA-based grouping and adaptive rank allocation effectively compress KV cache, but the strategy's applicability depends on the attention architecture (MHA vs. GQA).

title: From Cognitive Architectures to Language Agents: A Mechanism-Level Review of Lineage, Convergence, and Migration Gaps
summary: Memory, planning, reflection, and tool use are often compared as feature labels, obscuring the control semantics that determine how an agent actually runs. This review connects ten historical cognitive architectures, eight language-agent runtime families, and forty-two mechanism-focused modern systems. We reconstruct each mechanism through state, control, transition, persistence, failure, learning, and resource governance, then code evidence relation (E1-E4) separately from migration depth (D0-D4). The resulting landscape is uneven. Modern agents have operationalized substantial parts of adaptive memory, failure recovery, dynamic team selection, workflow search, skill induction, resource scheduling, and uncertainty-conditioned action, although often through independent convergence rather than documented inheritance. The strongest remaining opportunities lie in couplings among mechanisms. Closest-baseline screening closes one proposed gap: GraSP already combines calibrated multi-skill selection, typed compilation, verification, bounded repair, and replanning or ReAct fallback. Five residual bundles remain: activation with latency and action utility; typed impasse with isolated substates and resolution compilation; bounded content competition with broadcast and admission learning; persistent intention with reconsideration and live method authority; and uncertainty with resource allocation, interruption, and stopping. We contribute a distinctive-mechanism catalog, an auditable evidence-depth framework, and a falsifiable agenda for testing these bundles as composable runtime invariants.

AI.tldr: This paper systematically compares historical and modern cognitive architectures and agent runtimes, revealing an uneven landscape where mechanisms like memory, planning, and tool use are often independently rediscovered. It identifies five key mechanism bundles that remain underexplored and proposes a falsifiable agenda for testing them as composable runtime invariants.
AI.motivation: Current agent research uses vague feature labels (e.g., "memory," "planning," "reflection") that obscure the actual control semantics of how agents operate.
